South Korea's liberal President Lee Jae Myung says he’ll underscore the need for a practical, step-by-step denuclearization of North Korea during this week’s U.N. General Assembly, adding that both Seoul and Washington are willing to reengage with Pyongyang.

“To change the direction of a moving vehicle, it must be brought to a halt first,” Lee said in written responses to questions by The Associated Press before his departure Monday to New York. “A phased approach of stop, reduction and dismantlement is a practical way of effectively resolving the North Korean nuclear issue.”

Lee's push comes as North Korea is ramping up weapons testing activities even after U.S. President Donald Trump scaled back a major military exercise with South Korea in a conciliatory gesture toward leader Kim Jong Un, who viewed it as an invasion rehearsal.

Lee advocates phased denuclearization of North Korea

North Korea's evolving nuclear program has raised questions about whether its denuclearization can be achieved in a single step and given rise to calls for convincing North Korea to denuclearize in phases in return for corresponding economic and political benefits. Trump claimed last month that North Korea has 57 nuclear weapons, while some experts say the North has more than 100 warheads.

“Given the extent to which North Korea’s nuclear and missile capabilities have advanced, it is not a realistic solution to wait until complete denuclearization can be achieved all at once," Lee said. “This is because, in the interim, North Korea’s nuclear capabilities will continue to advance, escalating the threat.”

During the annual U.N. gathering, Lee said he would pursue “a phased and pragmatic solution to the North Korean nuclear issue” and build on his vision for promoting peace on the Korean Peninsula. Lee cited his recent offer for talks among concerned parties to formally end the 1950-53 Korean War, through which he said ways to curb North Korea's nuclear program could be explored.

There are concerns that a phased approach could eventually result in North Korea refusing to fully abandon its nuclear program after winning what it wants — like sanctions relief — in return for a partial surrender of its capability.

To prevent that, Lee called for comprehensive dialogue to establish a framework that benefits South Korea, the U.S. and North Korea alike, and stressed the need to show North Korea that “moving toward stable and lasting peace is a realistic and feasible path to a secure and prosperous future.”

South Korea, US want resumption of talks with North Korea

Whatever approach the U.S., South Korea and their partners take, it's unclear whether North Korea would return to talks anytime soon.

When Trump, citing a “very good relationship” with Kim, scaled back the annual Ulchi Freedom Shield exercise with South Korea last month, North Korea dismissed Trump's outreach, saying that just cutting the drill won't change its provocative nature. It has since performed three rounds of weapons launch events and unleashed numerous statements criticizing what it called U.S. hostilities. Experts say North Korea likely wants bigger U.S. concessions.

Lee, who hopes a resumption of Trump-Kim diplomacy would lead to reopening dialogue between the two Koreas, called Trump’s action “a deliberate step to send a clear message that the United States has no hostile intent toward North Korea.” He said both South Korea and the U.S. “remain open to engaging in dialogue with North Korea without preconditions.”

“What is needed now is a political decision at the leaders’ level. The two leaders should build trust and work together to identify a common ground, face-to-face,” Lee said.

Lee intends to strengthen ties with US

Trump's social media post on the exercise's downsizing came without prior consultations with South Korea, and mentioned what he called Lee's refusal to join the U.S. in the “denuclearization” of Iran. This raised worries about the alliance between South Korea and the U.S.

Lee admitted Trump's decision came “somewhat unexpectedly.” But Lee said he would rather focus on the ultimate objective behind that decision, saying Trump expressed his commitment to creating conditions conducive to dialogue and that he shares the goal of reducing confrontation on the Korean Peninsula.

Lee said the strategic interests of South Korea and the U.S. are deeply intertwined across a wide range of areas and that he intends to build a more mutually beneficial partnership during the rest of Trump's term. For example, Lee said planned cooperation in shipbuilding will not only revitalize U.S. shipbuilding and naval power but also create new growth opportunities for South Korean businesses.

Lee said Friday that he won't let his military be drawn into the U.S.-Iran conflict. He said his government was considering expanding the operations of a naval unit deployed in the Gulf of Aden to protect South Korean vessels and oil shipping routes. Lee was expected to meet Trump on the sidelines of the U.N. meeting.

Lee calls for UN reforms

Lee said the U.N.-centered multilateral system faces serious challenges, including intensifying geopolitical conflicts. He said the existing multilateral system is failing to keep pace with common challenges like the climate crisis and the unintended consequences of the AI revolution.

Calling for reforms at the U.N., Lee said redundancy and inefficiency across the organization must be addressed. He said greater authority must be granted to those working in the field, so that crises can be tackled swiftly and effectively.

During the U.N. General Assembly, Lee said he'll also present South Korea's push for more people to benefit from AI advances and call on other countries to join the effort.

Lee refrains from stating definite view on Kim's daughter

Asked about the prominent teenage daughter of the 42-year-old North Korean leader, Lee said that his government has taken note of “her rising status" and is keeping all possibilities open over her.

But Lee said “however, I believe we have to be careful about expressing a definite view at this stage.”

Lee's comments stand in contrast to the repeated assessments by South Korea's spy agency, which described her as Kim's likely heir. Some experts disagree with that view, citing North Korea's male-dominated power hierarchy system.

FIFA President Gianni Infantino has indicated he'd be open to an independent review of its governance system and signaled a willingness to consider reforms.

Facing intense scrutiny and criticism following the failure of the “ FIFA Forward Enterprise ” (FFE) project, Infantino sent a letter on Monday outlining this proposal to all FIFA Council members and the 211 member associations ahead of the next FIFA Council meeting scheduled for Oct. 15.

“I will ask the Council whether it wishes to commission an external, independent assessment of FIFA’s current governance framework for major strategic initiatives and to recommend potential improvements,” Infantino stated in his letter, which was seen by The Associated Press.

“I will propose that the Council establish a direct, structured, and time-bound consultation with the confederations and member associations on how to further strengthen FIFA’s decision-making processes,” he added.

Backlash over private investors plan

Under the FIFA Forward Enterprise concept, private investors would have purchased shares in the World Cup and other competitions.

However, the project leaked publicly sooner than Infantino had anticipated, sparking sharp criticism and creating a rift among member associations. Some of the most high-profile members — including several from European soccer body UEFA — withdrew their support for Infantino.

“The proposal entered the public domain before FIFA’s planned institutional process had been completed and before it could be presented in full to the Council and the member associations. I recognize that, without full context, this caused concern and created the impression that decisions had already been taken. They had not,” Infantino said in the letter.

Legal pressure, strategic ambitions

The fallout has escalated beyond internal disagreement. Last month, UEFA started drafting criminal charges against Infantino in U.S. courts regarding the FFE plan, requesting the release of all relevant documents.

Despite the controversy, Infantino continues to champion the goal of generating more revenue for world football’s governing body.

“Withdrawing this proposal does not diminish our ambition or our responsibility to reinvest a greater share of the fruits of FIFA’s success into football. We will continue to explore sustainable ways to increase FIFA’s resources,” Infantino added. “What changes is not the ambition, but the strength of the process.”

This governance crisis comes at a crucial political time for FIFA’s leadership. In March 2027, the 56-year-old FIFA chief will run for office for a fourth time, while any prospective rivals have until Nov. 18 to submit a candidate to challenge him.

The debate over the absence of promotion and relegation in Mexican soccer reached the floor of the Senate on Monday, where officials announced that a legislative reform to restore the system will be proposed on Tuesday.

Sen. Clemente Castañeda of the Movimiento Ciudadano party put forward the proposal, backed by representatives from other party leaderships, including Ignacio Mier of the ruling Morena party.

Castañeda stated that the initiative is critical for “expressly incorporating sporting merit among the obligations that national sports associations must observe” and ensuring promotion and relegation are enshrined in Mexican law.

“When they closed off the possibility of promotion, they didn’t just change a sporting rule; they also restricted a path for players, staff, and sports projects to grow in a country that needs to open up opportunities,” Castañeda said.

The senator said that they invited the president of the Liga MX, Francisco Iturbide, and the commissioner of the Mexican football, Mikel Arriola, and they declined.

The Associated Press reached out to the Mexican Federation for comment but did not get a response.

Broken Promises and Second-Division Issues

Owners of Mexican top-flight teams eliminated promotion and relegation in April 2020, citing financial difficulties among second-division clubs that were exacerbated by the coronavirus pandemic.

Under the original plan, the suspension was set for five years, with the system scheduled for reinstatement last year so that a team could earn promotion and another face relegation at the end of the most recent season in May of this year.

However, reinstatement never materialized. Starting last year, several second-division clubs began protesting to demand that authorities honor the agreement. At the time, the Mexican Football Federation stated that returning to the system was impossible because the necessary economic conditions did not yet exist.

“The whole pandemic thing was a sham; they always knew they were going to permanently shut down promotion and relegation,” said Alberto Castellanos, president of U. de G., one of the protesting teams.

High Barriers and Disillusioned Investors

Liga MX imposed stringent requirements on second-division teams, mandating a certification process before they could aspire to play in the top tier. These rules included a venue capacity requirement of 30,000 seats — a standard not even met by all active first-division clubs.

The elimination of promotion directly impacted new investors in Mexican soccer. Cancún FC was acquired in 2022 by an investment group led by figures like former Houston Astros general manager Jeff Luhnow on the premise that promotion would return.

“When we bought the team, we saw great potential — potential that often even Mexicans don’t see—but the current system fosters mediocrity; it’s very sad,” said Giovani Solazzi, the team’s president.

Facing pushback from certain second-division owners, Mexican soccer authorities completely removed the promotion and relegation system from the regulations this year. Neither the Federation nor Liga MX provided an explanation for the decision.

Top-Flight Perspective and Public Outcry

The owner of Club América — one of Mexico’s most powerful clubs and arguably its most influential decision-maker — stated last month that he supports reinstating the system, provided the right conditions are met.

“I am in favor of promotion and relegation. Everyone makes comparisons, pointing out that it exists in Spain, England, or Portugal; however, those countries have very solid second divisions, whereas here, we haven’t managed to build that kind of solid second-division league,” he said.

Once promotion was officially scrapped, widespread protests broke out during second-division matches. Players responded on the pitch by standing motionless after the opening whistle or passing the ball passively without attacking.

“I arrived in Mexico on June 8 under the premise that there would be promotion — joining Morelia, a team contending for promotion —- but then we were notified that it wasn’t happening,” said Spanish goalkeeper Roberto Galán. “That’s why we protested and the clubs were sanctioned, but the protests will continue because we have the right to make our voices heard.”

Fan groups have also shown up at stadiums wearing protest shirts to voice their discontent.

And last week, Mexico’s National Antitrust Commission (CNA) launched an investigation into potential monopolistic practices in the Mexican league centering on the absence of a promotion and relegation system.

___

Armando Solís contributed to this report from Morelia, México.

News.title: ‘42 surgeries in 48 hours’: Doctors face extreme pressure in South Sudan
News.content:
Dr Mathiang Agany had no idea what was coming.

On a humid morning in April, scores of patients were rushed into his basic hospital in rural South Sudan after a shoot out between rival gangs. As the most senior doctor, Dr Agany, a maternal health specialist, had to perform 42 surgeries in just 48 hours.

Working alongside a second surgeon, a nurse and an anaesthetist, Dr Agany, 44, carefully extracted bullets from the vital organs of nine patients.

In 22 cases, he glued together fractured bones; and in four others he clamped damaged tissues shut and repaired torn organs.

Over the same 48 hour period, he also delivered seven babies through emergency c-sections.

“You are tired... but you can relax later,” he told The Telegraph over a video call.

“My job [was] to keep people alive”.

Separate to the ruinous four-year civil war in neighbouring Sudan, the violence plaguing South Sudan is inter-communal, a self-perpetuating cycle of cattle raiding, territorial disputes and revenge attacks carried out by armed youth militias from pastoral communities known as Titweng (“cattle guard”).

Young children were among the victims, including a four-year-old boy, whose leg was fractured by a gunshot, and a nine-month-old baby girl whose chest was grazed by the same bullet that killed her father.

News.title: Afghan medical students face expulsion from Pakistan
News.content:
An educational lifeline for young Afghan women banned by the Taliban from training as doctors in their homeland is in jeopardy after Pakistan’s medical authorities tried to have them expelled.

Several hundred Afghan female students studying across the border in Pakistan have been threatened with removal, amid rising tensions and tit-for-tat exchanges between the neighbours.

The Pakistan Medical and Dental Council (PMDC) which regulates medical education earlier this month ordered medical and dental colleges with Afghan students to kick them out.

Within days, major institutions including King Edward Medical University (KEMU), Shaikh Khalifa Bin Zayed Al Nahyan Medical and Dental College, and the Services Institute of Medical Sciences, had ordered Afghan students to leave.

The nationwide order was estimated to have affected around 1,000 Afghan students, with 35 per cent of those thought to be female students.

Provincial high courts have now temporarily halted the expulsion pending further hearings, but Afghan students told The Telegraph they were terrified their careers would be ended.

“The government’s decision aimed to send us to the Stone Age because the Taliban in Afghanistan have banned female education,” said Sabiha Daftani, one of the 22 Afghan students given orders on September 7 by KEMU in Lahore on to leave within 24 hours.

“The fear is constant and haunting us,” she said.

News.title: Michael Carrick will not survive unless Manchester United change
News.content:
But so passive was their football that is the way he felt in the moment. For a club with United’s “attack, attack, attack” tradition – becoming something of a distant memory as seasons pass – that is a damning as it gets.

Neville’s Sky paymasters will be delighted by his emotive, insulting, headline-grabbing language. But he of course exaggerated a point to make a point. United, and Carrick, were, indeed, far too passive, lacking aggression, urgency and belief. They just do not press. United did, for too long, play like a team of dummies.

Against Fulham they almost played walking football until they conceded, desperation kicked in and they chased the game to salvage a late draw.

It begs the question: what is Carrick doing with this team? Yes, he may have been let down by no defensive signings in the summer – even if he must have bought into the plan to prioritise a midfield rebuild – but he is far from absolved from blame.

He will cling to the response to Lisandro Martínez’s own goal, to striking a post twice in the first half from Matheus Cunha and Bruno Fernandes, to managing to avoid a third successive defeat in a week, which would have led to the crisis klaxon being sounded. Carrick can talk about how ridiculous it would be to question his position as head coach. But is it?

We now go into a three-week international break and the Premier League vacuum would have been filled by a debate over Carrick’s future, whether he is up to the job and another existential examination as to where United are heading. And who is to blame.

That still might happen. United did not lose. But they were not remotely good enough, as has been the case for most of the season. Their only league win in five was against newly promoted Ipswich Town, having lost to newly promoted Hull City. They have also drawn at Everton and now at Fulham, who started the day bottom of the table and remain winless. Apart from facing Manchester City, it has hardly been the most taxing of starts. Except they are down in 12th and have not played well at all.

News.title: Alisson’s brilliance takes the breath away to show way forward for Liverpool
News.content:
It proved to be the foundation stone from which Liverpool were able to build and inflict Bournemouth’s first home defeat since January. There are plenty of [valid] questions to ask of Liverpool’s attack at present but, defensively, it is starting to come together.

“It was a really good fight,” Alisson said, in that self-effacing way of his. “But we have to improve a lot – on the ball and sometimes off the ball as well but we improved in the second half. We adapted to the opponent and that’s what we are doing.”

Any manager with a well-drilled defence stands a chance of improving and that is what Liverpool are doing. Only four weeks ago the discussion was about how easy it was for teams to play through their middle – remember that chaotic afternoon at Newcastle to start? – but that is changing swiftly.

Since Iraola replaced Jeremie Frimpong with Araújo at right-back, three consecutive Premier League clean sheets have followed. Araújo, the Uruguayan on loan from Barcelona, revels in doing the dirty work while Jacquet, the £60m signing from Rennes, oozes quality.

“He’s [Jacquet] very young and adapted really well to the Premier League,” Iraola said. “The first games, he was physically feeling the change of rhythm and I had to sub him. This was a step forward. He looked solid until the end. He’s in a good place physically and I hope he can continue his development.”

News.title: All that money spent and Spurs do not have a proper striker or goalkeeper
News.content:
It was an excellent goal, but Kinsky got a good hand to it and a top goalkeeper would have pushed it around the post. On the evidence of the first half, when he made four saves, Suzuki would have also stopped the ball creeping into the net.

Suzuki cost Villa in the region of £30m and he looks a more than able replacement for Emiliano Martínez. Spurs, on the other hand, have not had a top-class goalkeeper since Hugo Lloris and it is a puzzle that so much faith has been placed in Kinsky.

Spurs spent most of the summer firmly denying any links to Jackson before Villa signed him from Chelsea for an initial £47.5m that could rise to £65m. Given the London club paid an initial £75m for Sávio and committed to a £60m obligation to make Omar Marmoush’s season-long loan permanent, Jackson might have been a relative bargain for them.

Asked if Tottenham had made a big mistake by failing to sign a proper number nine, head coach Robert De Zerbi said: “The transfer market was long. The situation changed many times. There was also the financial rules, at the end of the transfer market. And we had to respect the rules.

“We didn’t sell the players who we thought, in the beginning, there was the possibility, the chance to sell. There are a lot of reasons. I think the club and the coach, we are not sleeping, we know the characteristics of the players, we know everything. And if we didn’t make any different decisions, it was because we couldn’t.”

News.title: An A to Z guide to what’s in your laundry detergent
News.content:
Laundry is one of those jobs that most of us do on autopilot. Throw a load of washing and your favourite detergent into the drum and wait for the machine to work its magic. Perhaps you’ve never even thought to ask yourself what chemicals you’re putting in with your clothes.

In the UK, detergent brands are legally required to state the use of surfactants and enzymes (the main ingredients for stain removal) in a way that is easy to understand, but you may see additional compounds that leave you scratching your head.

Here, I break down the words on the back of the bottle to help you understand exactly what you’re putting in your washing. Given that I’ve just tested 26 laundry detergents and developed an app to help you clean your clothes better, I’m the best woman for the job.

Below, you’ll find the most common detergent ingredients listed A to Z. If you’ve got a burning question about a laundry buzzword, I should be able to help. Add any in the comments section below.

Anionic

There are two main types of surfactants: anionic and non-ionic. A surfactant has a hydrophilic head that loves water and a hydrophobic tail that hates it. Anionic surfactants have a negative charge on their head, which is what helps lift soils and stains from the fabric, though they’re not so good at getting rid of oils. They create a lot of foam but their effectiveness can be limited by minerals found in hard water, which is why they are paired with non-ionic surfactants.

Bio

Short for biological, this label means that a detergent contains enzymes. These are proteins that break down fats, starches and grease, so use bio formulations when you need to tackle stubborn food stains. They are effective at lower temperatures but they can be abrasive on sensitive skin. If your skin is easily irritated, opt for non-bio, instead.

News.title: Spitting row mars feisty Millwall-West Ham clash
News.content:
Millwall manager Alex Neil said after the game that fourth official Lewis Smith had confirmed a spitting accusation had been made.

Asked if he had spoken to Marschall about the claim, Neil replied: “I haven’t asked him about it. But it’s like anything else; I’m sure there’ll be footage of it, or not of it, if it didn’t happen.

“I’d be extremely surprised if Fil’s made an accusation and nothing’s happened. But that’s not really for me to deal with; I’m sure the authorities will deal with that.”

West Ham manager Nuno Espírito Santo said: “I’m aware of the allegation. I didn’t see the image; I didn’t speak with Taty. I cannot go much further on that.”

He added: “I’m going to try to look at the images.”

There were also ugly scenes at full time when players had to be separated at the end of a derby that had been at the centre of an unprecedented police operation.

There were six arrests as of 4pm on Saturday for offences including tailgating, assault on a police officer and entering or attempting to enter a stadium while intoxicated.

News.title: Bloodthirsty Brighton feast on rattled Arsenal
News.content:
Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of today’s Premier League 3pm kick-offs, with Brighton vs Arsenal the pick of the three matches.

Brighton are the league’s top goalscorers so far this season and have amassed the most expected goals, but the champions have the league’s best defence and are seeking five wins from five to start their title defence. There is some welcome needle between Fabian Hurzeler and Mikel Arteta, dating back to Declan Rice’s contentious second yellow for delaying the restart two years ago, as well as the Brighton manager’s comments about Arsenal’s style of play in March.

That 1-0 Arsenal victory at the Amex coincided with Man City dropping points at home to Nottingham Forest on a pivotal night in the title race. Bukayo Saka scored a deflected shot in the ninth minute, and Arsenal held on from there in an ugly but resolute display.

With Saka, Martin Odegaard and Kai Havertz fit and firing, as well as the introduction of Myles Lewis-Skelly and Bruno Guimaraes to Arteta’s midfield stable, Arsenal’s football has been more technical and enterprising so far this season. Brighton are one of the few teams who will back themselves to play through Arsenal’s press, which should make for an absorbing game.

Elsewhere, Newcastle are looking to bounce back from their shellacking at Leeds at home to surprise package Hull City. Mattias Jaissle’s team took four points from Liverpool and Spurs but there is concern about how many shots they are conceding. Hull remain unbeaten and continue to confound the odds and underlying data, but that surely cannot last forever.

Everton are also one of the division’s unbeaten teams, but will be targeting three points from a home game against Ipswich after three consecutive draws. Sports.title: Andros Townsend says ‘I thought my ankle was going to snap’ as he speaks on ‘terrifying’ moment roller ran him over

ANDROS TOWNSEND has revealed he thought his ankle was going to “snap” when he was run over by a roller.

The former Premier League and England star is currently playing his football out in Thailand.



Townsend, 35, is contracted to Thai League 1 side Prachuap but was caught in an unfortunate accident on Friday night.

During half-time of the clash against Pattani he was run over by one of the two pitch rollers.



Footage of the terrifying incident went viral on social media with many fans concerned for the ex-Tottenham and Everton winger.

Fortunately, Townsend escaped with just a few scratches and was able to play in the game as a substitute.



He has now spoken about the incident during an appearance on Piers Morgan Unsenscored.

He said: “I didn’t see it coming.

“It was at half-time, we were going out to warm up. I saw two rollers on either side of the pitch.

“I remember thinking to myself, ‘I’ve never seen that before in my career, what are they doing?’

“But we got called to warm up. Didn’t think anything of it.

“The next I saw him was when I was literally underneath him and thankfully no serious damage.

“A couple of bumps and bruises but managed to walk away unscathed, luckily.

“Every time I see it, I’m cringing, I’m in disbelief. When I sent it to my kids, my kids thought it was AI.



“Literally, I had to explain to them, for the next ten minutes, that it was real.

“It’s horrible to watch back and to see what could have been but.

“Thankfully, I was fortunate I did manage to fall onto the floor at the right time, so nothing snapped as the roller went over me.

Sports.title: Ten mistakes Michael Carrick has made that could cost him his job at Man Utd including Rashford and Cunha blunders
Sports.content:
Next

MANCHESTER UNITED have already dropped almost as many points under Michael Carrick this season as they did last season.

Since the opening weekend horror show at Hull, much of what Carrick has said and done has been unbecoming of a United coach or manager.



Matchgoers started to turn at Fulham when they booed his removal of Kobbie Mainoo in the 90th minute. Even Carrick’s ghostwriter questioned him in an online post.

Substituting Mainoo was not an obvious mistake but Carrick has made plenty in the first month of the campaign and it could yet cost him.



After two wins from seven games, here is where Carrick has gone wrong:

Starting Heaven at Hull

Hull was hell for Ayden Heaven, who has not started in the Premier League since United’s 2-0 loss on August 22.

Heaven started in all six pre-season games, purely through his left-footedness. With Lisandro Martinez unavailable following his World Cup commitments, Carrick turned to the only other leftie at centre half.

Pitting the 19-year-old Heaven against Oli McBurnie was a major misjudgement. Choosing Noussair Mazraoui or Diogo Dalot is a toss of a coin but Mazraoui was patently not ready to start at right back at the MKM Stadium.

Starting Dorgu on the left at Hull

United have three left wingers and Patrick Dorgu is the weakest, yet he lined up at Hull on the back of a full pre-season.

Dorgu’s day lasted 45 minutes. Carrick had a blindspot with the Denmark international, on the scoresheet in the United head coach’s first two games back in charge in January. He now seems to have opened his eyes to Dorgu’s limitations.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Man Utd ratings v Fulham MANCHESTER UNITED salvaged a 1-1 draw as Fulham narrowly missed out on their first Premier League win of the season. Matheus Cunha’s late deflected strike saved United from a first defeat at Craven Cottage since 2009. Lisandro Martinez’s embarrassing own goal after Senne Lammens parried out Calvin Bassey‘s shot in the 63rd minute summed up a dreadful afternoon for the Red Devils. Here’s how SunSport’s Katherine Walsh rated the outrun United players at a sunny Craven Cottage.

By playing Dorgu on the left wing, Matheus Cunha went up front when Bryan Mbeumo had played the entirety of pre-season there. The planning went out the window.

Playing Cunha up front

Look at Cunha’s goal against Fulham again and note where he receives the ball. On the left wing, where he played every time he appeared for Carrick last season.

This season, Cunha has moved to the tip of the arrow and not been as sharp. Mbeumo, who scored every time he had a stint up front for Carrick last term, has returned to the right wing.

That is partly due to the absence of Amad through injury yet switching Dorgu to the right was worth a go at some stage, if only to have two of United’s most threatening forwards in roles they thrived in in the second half of last season.



Substituting Rashford at Everton

Carrick said Rashford “felt something” with United 1-0 up at Everton. Fair enough. But removing him for Dorgu sent out the wrong signal.

Everton, becoming increasingly dominant, had sent on an actual left winger in Jack Grealish and received an adrenaline shot. They equalised.

Rashford had requested an energy gel, so if he absolutely had to go off then Benjamin Sesko should have replaced him.

Cunha could have shifted to the left to accommodate the striker and signal United’s attacking intent.



Substituting Shaw at Everton

Dalot had gone off for Leny Yoro after Everton made it 1-1. Luke Shaw then made way for Mazraoui in added time, minutes after United had regained their lead.

Shaw would go on to miss three games yet he had four more minutes to see out at the Hill Dickinson Stadium and overlapped to cross for Sesko’s goal in the 88th minute.

Dalot was hooked as he was on a booking. From Carrick’s viewpoint, withdrawing book full backs may have been enforced, though that is debatable.

The knock-on effect was ruinous. Yoro, a centre back, was narrow and afforded Grealish too much room to pick out Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall.



Mazraoui, conscious of fouling Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall inside the area, did not fully commit to the tackle and unwittingly teed up Ainsley Maitland-Niles to sweep in a spectacular 95th-minute leveller.

Not sending Sesko on sooner against City

Phil Foden’s 23rd-minute red card gave Carrick 22 minutes to assess 11-versus-10. United made little headway with the man advantage and lacked a focal point against a City back four that comprised three centre backs.

Sesko warmed up at the start of the second half. The Stretford End chanted his name. He did not come on for another 19 minutes.

By then, Erling Haaland had scored the only goal of the game. Carrick’s only other attempt at game-changing was to introduce the harmless Joshua Zirkzee.



Moving Fernandes into midfield against City

When Sesko crossed the white line, it was for Youri Tielemans. Cunha withdrew into the hole and Bruno Fernandes dropped further back into midfield.

Fernandes has had some brilliant games in a deeper role yet moving him farther from the City goal with 20-odd minutes remaining and United trailing was counter-productive.

United did not have a sniff until Bryan Mbeumo was played in by Fernandes in the 95th minute. Fernandes was occupying the space that a No.10 operates in.

Too many changes against Brighton

Brighton had won at Old Trafford four seasons running. United have won two trophies in nine years and went out of both domestic cup competitions at the first hurdle last season.



It was not the night for eight changes, never mind the inclusion of a 15-year-old on the bench.

After much talk, JJ Gabriel never got his call-up after telling United he wanted to leave the club.

But starting Yoro and Heaven in front of debutant goalkeeper Karl Darlow asked for trouble and United got it. The trio were culpable for all three goals as Brighton became the first team to win at Old Trafford from 2-0 down since Tottenham in September 1976.

Repeatedly turning to Zirkzee

Since his two goals in Ruben Amorim’s first Premier League win on December 1 2024, Joshua Zirkzee has scored two Premier League goals.

United were prepared to offload him in the summer and Everton came calling on deadline day. United decided they needed the extra body.



Zirkzee has subsequently emerged in three games with United losing. Carrick has been without Amad and Sesko was missing again at Fulham but he needs to be more imaginative than summoning a flop. Zirkzee has done nowt.

Reverting to the same XI at Fulham

Carrick picked the same starting XI against Ipswich Town, Everton and Fulham. A win, a draw and a near-defeat.

Even the 5-2 victory against Ipswich had dollops of good fortune. United seized on a slip for their equalising goal and there was a handball from Harry Maguire for their second.



The back four in those games was Dalot, Maguire, Martinez and Shaw. David Moyes did the legwork on the Shaw deal that was signed off by Louis van Gaal in 2014. Jose Mourinho signed Dalot. Maguire was Solskjaer’s signing and Martinez followed Erik ten Hag to Old Trafford.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

That was the back four in the 4-0 drubbing by Brentford in August 2022, United’s worst-ever performance in the Premier League era.

Carrick’s United have sieved five goals in four games with the quartet and it could have been more.

Sports.title: Gianni Infantino buckles under Uefa pressure as Fifa President offers major concession after World Cup chaos
Sports.content:
Next

FIFA boss Gianni Infantino buckled under Uefa pressure as he offered a full independent review of the world body’s governance model.

European, Asian and Concacaf bosses are demanding the Swiss resigns in the wake of the failed scheme to sell off the World Cup to private investors.



National associations including the FA are also seeking a formal probe into Infantino’s role in US striker Folarin Balogun’s red card reversal this summer, after pressure from US President Donald Trump.

And in a clear sign that Infantino is feeling the heat, the leader of the global game has now offered to meet his critics half-way.



In a letter to all 211 member nations and Fifa’s ruling Council, Infantino said: “First, I will ask the Council whether it wishes to commission an independent external review of Fifa’s current governance framework for major strategic initiatives and recommend potential improvements.

“Second, I will propose that the Council establish a direct, structured and time-limited consultation with confederations, Member Associations and relevant stakeholders on how Fifa’s decision-making can be further strengthened.”



The letter, with a vow to “strengthen transparency, participation and accountability in major strategic initiatives” comes with Fifa facing THREE separate legal processes lodged by Uefa in the US.

Infantino claimed that the Fifa Forward Enterprises plan “did not involve relinquishing Fifa’s control or authority over sporting decisions.”

He added: “The proposal entered the public domain before Fifa’s planned institutional process had been completed.

“I recognise that, without the full context, this caused concern and created the impression that decisions had already been taken.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

“They had not.

“It remained a proposal, not a decision, and was always subject to the necessary approvals of the Council and the Member Associations. It has now been withdrawn and will not proceed.

“Fifa’s democratic processes, independence and sporting authority were never for sale. They are not for sale and never will be.”

It is unlikely that Infantino’s opponents will back down with the latest step seen by many as a sign of weakness, although so far he still does not have a declared opponent for March’s Presidential election, with less than two months to the deadline for candidates to file.

Sports.title: Why Tottenham MUST keep faith with De Zerbi’s tactics despite being rock bottom of Premier League
Sports.content:
Next

TOTTENHAM entered the three-week international break BOTTOM of the Premier League following a disastrous start to the season.

Saturday’s 3-2 home defeat to Aston Villa left them with just two points from their opening five games.



Spurs’ start to the campaign could reasonably lead to questions regarding their manager Roberto De Zerbi.

But it is not time to panic just yet.



Spurs lead the league in several statistical categories, including successful take-ons, progressive passes and corners – although they are 18th in expected goals.

Despite their blunt attack and lack of points, there are tactical reasons for Tottenham fans to remain optimistic.



Bermuda triangle

De Zerbi is working in triangles. You can see that there’s work on the training ground happening because they’ve got players in positions to receive the ball and make it difficult for defences.

And there are line-breaking passes going between the lines into people’s feet. It’s not chaotic, it’s structured.

You’ve got a deep lying triangle that they’re dictating play from. And then you’ve got players in between the lines in positions to affect play higher up the field. It’s well-drilled, and it’s well-coached.

I want them to get a bit higher up the field in more of a 3-1-6 and change that around slightly. But it’s not as bad as you might think it is.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Line breakers

They’ve got this linebreaking pass about to happen, but those Bermuda triangles, as we’ve called them, out wide, creating a problem for the opposition here, OK? So they’ve created a problem for Aston Villa here by pinning these players over with this triangle on that side.

Those bermuda triangles, as we’ve called them, caused problems for Aston Villa on Saturday – and there were plenty of line-breaking passes into the likes of Mateus Fernandes.

I don’t really want to see Fernandes as the number 10, but in this position he does manage to get himself between the lines.

However, when you look at Spurs’ pass map, it really is quite telling.



This is not a team that should be bottom of the league. They’re creating chances, high on possession stats, carrying the ball, they have dribblers.

They’ve transformed these areas of their game, without yet being rewarded.

Deep flyer tactics

Last season, Tottenham couldn’t get out of their defensive third. They can now, as they’re being well coached.



The next bit, however, is creating more of a synergy between their attacking players when they do get into good positions.

So many times this season thus far, Spurs have gotten into dangerous areas without capitalising, at times failing to even getting a shot away.

But with more time for signings to gel, the likes of Omar Marmoush and Savio may get more in sync with their team-mates.

Spurs have turned opponents around and got sprinters running behind, they’ve got those high flyers.

But they’re not releasing the ball into these positions to send them away.

They’re creating opportunities, but not turning those into high end chances.

More minutes for James Maddison can make a difference, as he has the vision to play killer passes that others, including makeshift No10 Fernandes, have missed.

Sports.title: Rangers hero Ally McCoist broke my leg on Australia pub crawl – I feared my career was OVER
Sports.content:
Next

EVER since the idea of writing my autobiography came about, I’ve been dreading this aspect of it — the true story of how I broke my leg.

But it’s been 40 years since the incident and I’m pretty sure enough time has passed for the truth to be told.



The truth is that it was a drunken altercation with Ally McCoist — and it was all my own fault.

Rangers boss Jock Wallace had arranged a tour to New Zealand and Australia for the end of the 1983-84 season.



Our first game was a 0-0 draw against an Australian B side in Melbourne and I had to make do with a place on the bench.

Next stop Brisbane. On arrival, we discovered that Manchester United were also touring there and Big Jock and the United boss, Ron Atkinson, got talking.



It turned out United were staying in a place called Surfers Paradise. It sounded brilliant and, if it was good enough for them, it was good enough for us.

We had been given an evening pass from the boss and everybody was up for a night out.

As the night progressed, we started getting separated. I found myself with Craig Paterson, Ally Dawson and Coisty.

We had left one pub and were looking for our next watering hole. We didn’t have a clue where we were going and found ourselves walking down this really wide road.



OUR BEST FREE BETS & SIGN-UP OFFERS

We couldn’t see any sign of the bright lights of a pub, nor how we could get back to where we were staying, the Beachcomber Hotel.

As we discussed our next move, we thought we would take advantage of a grassy area to have a comfort break against one of the trees.

And as we were standing there, I began to joke with Coisty that I was going to ‘wash his shoes’, if you know what I mean.



I never did it, but one thing led to another and, before long, it was East Kilbride versus Easterhouse!

Perhaps, if we had been boxers, it would have been fists up, but we both kicked out with our feet, which resulted in an almighty clash of shins.

As I went down and landed on my backside I wasn’t in any pain, but I immediately knew something was wrong.

The other lads, Craig and Ally, were telling the two of us to get a move on.

I was lying on my back, my legs bent above me and I was thinking about getting up, but then I noticed something protruding from just below my knee.



I put my hand down and that was when I realised the thing sticking out was my bone, which had pierced through my skin.

The lads’ patience was, by now, wearing a bit thin, but as soon as they came over they immediately knew the only place I was going was to the hospital.

One of the lads went to phone an ambulance — the other had the dubious pleasure of going to inform Jock.

When Jock demanded an explanation, they were to say that they hadn’t seen anything.

This left me and Coisty alone, in the dark. He was a bit tearful as the full realisation of what had occurred began to register.



There might have been tears from me, too. I knew that this was a potentially career-threatening injury.

‘It wasn’t your fault,’ I said to him. ‘It was basically down to me’.

But Ally was distraught.

I then looked over and saw a nearby fence. And I knew exactly what I had to do.

‘Right,’ I said. ‘See that fence, I tried to jump it and I never made it. That’s what we’re going to say’.



But Ally was having none of it. He was adamant that, no matter the repercussions, he was going to tell the truth.

I knew that wasn’t a good idea. Ally was on his last warning and Jock’s patience with him was already wearing thin.

Any breach of rules and he was on the next plane home and, believe me, Jock would have done it.



Imagine if that had happened. Who knows what future Ally would have had at Rangers — if any?

Look what he went on to achieve at the club, the goals he scored, the trophies he won, the legend he became.

Was that really going to be put at risk because of some daft incident?

There was no way he should pay such a high price for what was my stupidity.

What had happened was no fault of Ally. It was all down to me.



It was my fault we had squared up but still he wanted to tell the truth.

So I said to Ally, ‘You don’t want to be doing that. You were on your last warning before we left London. No, you can’t do that. We’ll just say that I tried to jump the fence and didn’t make it. That’s what happened. I’m sure Craig and Ally will back that up’.

He took some convincing but, eventually, Ally came round to my way of thinking and Ally and big Craig stuck to the line that they didn’t see anything.

It was a story that would hold firm for four decades!

Big Jock caught up with us in the hospital when two nurses began trying to take off my trousers.



Even they were wincing when they tried to get my trousers over my leg.

It had swollen to twice the size and the bones were making a horrible grinding noise each time they hit.

Then, remarkably, Jock told me what happened, how my leg break had come about.

He said Coisty had told him everything, but, to my relief, he recounted the tale of me trying to jump the fence.

Then he paused. ‘Did Coisty top you?’ he asked.



My brain was working overtime. I was going to stick to our story no matter what.

‘No, I tried to jump a fence,’ I said. ‘It was further away than I thought. I landed on top of the thing and snapped my leg’.

Over the years, I have come to the conclusion that Big Jock knew the truth.



He felt there was some kind of undercurrent between me and Coisty, but I never felt it and I’m sure Ally didn’t.

But, at the time, I was laying there wondering how he could possibly know what had actually happened?

Jock looked at me. ‘Well’, he said. ‘If that’s the story you’re telling, you had better stick to it. I don’t want to hear anything else’.

I needed an operation and the surgeon told me he was confident he had done a good job, putting in a plate and some screws to hold everything in place.

But he didn’t know if I’d be able to continue with football, saying only that it was very much down to me and how the recovery developed.



I always believed I could get through it. I had to. There was no way I was going back on the tools.

I was determined not to let my career finish like that.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Out Of Easterhouse, The Bobby Williamson Story (Pitch Publishing), publishes on October 12. RRP £25.00.

Sports.title: World Cup stadium could be demolished to make way for 80,000-seater new arena
Sports.content:
Next

A FORMER World Cup stadium could be demolished to make way for a brand new 80,000-seater arena.

The Deutsche Bank Park was featured multiple times during the tournament in Germany in 2006.



The iconic ground was the setting for England‘s 1-0 victory over Paraguay and four other matches at that edition of the World Cup.

It has also been known as the Waldstadion, the Neues Waldstadion and the Commerzbank-Arena.



The Deutsche Bank Park was also used as a host stadium for other major tournaments such as the 1974 World Cup, the 2011 Women’s World Cup and Euro 2024.

Bundesliga club Eintracht Frankfurt are now planning to undertake a major expansion of the stadium.

This would see its capacity of 60,000 jump to a huge 80,000, which would make it the second largest in Germany.

It would trail Borussia Dortmund‘s Signal Iduna Park by just 1,365 seats.

Frankfurt spokesperson Axel Hellmann has revealed that two options are being considered.

One option would be to keep the current shell of the stadium and build a third tier on top of it.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

The second option would see the existing stadium demolished and a new state-of-the-art arena built on the same site.

A decision is yet to be made on which option will be selected by the 2022 Europa League winners.

Frankfurt are still carrying out research to assess the technical and economic feasibility of each plan.

The club has insisted that a more specific direction will be known in six months.



Hellmann has admitted that the project will not be a swift one to complete and suggested it could take over a decade before finishing.

The expansion would be expected to boost the stadium’s business with the possible addition of major concerts and other big events.

It could also become an important stadium if Germany are to win the hosting rights of future international tournaments.

Sports.content:
McLaren have confirmed they will bring more upgrades to this weekend's Azerbaijan Grand Prix, where they are expecting a four-way battle for victory with Mercedes, Ferrari and Red Bull.

After failing to claim a victory in the first 10 grands prix of the season, the reigning constructors' champions have come into form, with Lando Norris claiming three pole positions at the last four races and only being denied a third win by the unfortunate timing of a virtual safety car last time out in Madrid.

McLaren have once more exhibited strength in development, with regular upgrades brought to the MCL40 having played a significant part in catapulting them back into contention for victories.

The team's official preview for this weekend's race in Baku, which takes place on Saturday rather than the usual Sunday slot, revealed there will be new parts, and that their rotating 'H-Wing' will return to the car after not being used in Madrid.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Norris lost the lead of the Spanish GP after an unlucky sequence of events which saw a missed a pit-stop opportunity under a VSC, followed by a very slow stop

"As part of the team's continued journey throughout the 2026 season, the team will bring to Baku a set of upgrades aimed to improve the aerodynamic performance of the MCL40," the team said.

"Additionally the H-Wing, that debuted in Monza, will be back in action on a track where the drag reduction can be a factor.

"As has been the approach in previous races this season, all new parts will be evaluated throughout practice before the team makes final decisions regarding the MCL40's Qualifying and Grand Prix setup for the weekend."

McLaren chief technical officer and chief designer Rob Marshall explained the team are keen to continue their development push despite their title hopes being extremely thin, with Kimi Antonelli dominating the Drivers' Championship and his Mercedes team well clear in the constructors' standings.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch the moment Norris thought he messed up his lap, which turned out to put him on the pole for the Spanish Grand Prix

"With regulatory continuity into next season and the competition at the front so close, our motivation to keep developing the car remains high," Marshall said.

"We must balance that with work on next year's car, but our immediate focus is on delivering more performance and fighting for more victories in 2026, while carrying forward everything we learn."

The Baku circuit, which features the longest straight on the F1 calendar alongside several slow corners, creates a challenge that Marshall expects to create entertaining competition between the top teams.

"Baku will provide another valuable test of the MCL40 across a very different range of characteristics," Marshall added.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Norris reacts to the news that the Monaco Grand Prix will be a Sprint race in 2027

"Energy management and deployment will be particularly important, as will tyre and brake management with the cars arriving at Turn 1 after the long straight with these areas relatively cold.

"Operationally, there is very little margin for error on a tight street circuit. A small mistake can lead to significant repairs, lost track time and resources being diverted away from performance, so confidence, precision and disciplined execution will be essential throughout the weekend.

"We expect any of the top four teams to be capable of winning in Baku, with the chasing pack also getting closer, and we hope to be firmly in the fight at the front."

Sports.title: F1 race distances set to be reduced for 2027 season
Sports.content:
There is set to be a slight reduction in the length of Formula 1 races for the 2027 season, the FIA has confirmed.

At a meeting of the F1 Commission in London on Monday, the sport's decision makers agreed to reduce Grand Prix distances from 305km to 290km, which corresponds to a reduction of two to three laps depending on the circuit.

The change is being made because fuel flow rates are being increased next season as part of measures the FIA are introducing to optimise the all-new regulations brought in at the start of 2026.

The FIA said: "In line with the refinements to the Power Unit regulations to be introduced in 2027 on fuel flow, a reduction in the total race distance from 305km to 290km was approved, corresponding to a reduction of two or three laps."

The decision must be approved by the World Motor Sport Council, but that is expected to be a formality.

The FIA also announced slight changes to protocols around races disrupted by rain or other factors, with a three-hour limit (including interruptions) from race to start to finish removed, but a "hard stop" time for the end of any racing activity to be introduced.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the 2026 Spanish Grand Prix.

A limit of two hours of actual racing remains, with those decisions taken "to ensure that the spectators have the best possible chance to enjoy a full race if disruptions occur."

It was also confirmed that there will be "greater flexibility to extend Free Practice sessions should they be interrupted."

The current rules only allow for practice sessions to be extended on Sprint weekends, but such measures may now also be available on a regular schedule.

Sports.title: Wakefield's Guler set to miss rest of play-offs with ban for punching
Sports.content:
Wakefield prop Emre Guler is set to miss the rest of the Super League play-offs after being handed a two-match ban for punching.

The forward was sent off following a clash with Leigh's Owen Trout during Trinity's 26-16 victory over the Leopards in their eliminator last Friday.

The punishment was confirmed following a meeting of the Rugby Football League's match review panel on Monday.

Barring a successful appeal against the grade E offence, Guler will now miss Wakefield's semi-final against Wigan on Saturday and the Grand Final, if Trinity reach it.

Guler only joined Wakefield last month having brought forward his planned arrival from St George Illawarra Dragons from the start of the 2027 season.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Super League semi-final match between Wakefield Trinity and Leigh Leopards.

Team-mate Mike McMeeken will be free to play after being fined following a grade B charge of dangerous contact against Leigh's David Armstrong in the same game.

Warrington's James Harrison was also fined following a grade C charge of head contact in the Wolves' win over Hull KR, which set up a semi-final at Leeds. Team-mate Luke Yates will face no further action over a grade A dangerous throw.

Hull KR centre Peta Hiku has also been banned for two matches for punching Warrington's George Williams but, with Rovers now out of the play-offs, his suspension will be served next season.

Sports.content:
Atletico Madrid have hit back at Real Madrid's criticism of the referring decisions during the derby on Sunday.

Jose Mourinho arrived at the post-match press conference with printouts displaying two incidents he believed should have resulted in red cards to Atletico players.

What happened on Sunday?

Mourinho held up pictures of two tackles to the media after Real's defeat.

Mourinho strongly criticised the officials and was angry that Atletico defender Cristian Romero ‌was not sent off for a stamp on Jude Bellingham.

He also complained about a challenge by Lee Kang-in on Federico Valverde, before the visitors were reduced to 10 men five minutes after half-time.

"We could skip the press conference because the story of the match is right here," ​Mourinho said, holding up the images in what was the start of a near ‌five-minute rant.

"Those were two clear red cards. The difficulties we've faced since the sending-off - 11 against 10 - well, we can imagine what 50 ​minutes of 11 against nine would have been like if justice had been done."

Image: Real Madrid said the derby against Atletico Madrid was influenced by refereeing decisions

Real defender Dean Huijsen was dismissed for bringing down Giuliano Simeone inside the area as the last defender, allowing Alejandro Grimaldo to ​score with a low spot-kick.

Jonathan David doubled Atletico's lead six minutes later, ⁠with Antonio Rudiger heading in a free-kick late ⁠on to reduce the deficit.

Mourinho said he could only "hug" his players after what he described as a first half "full of class and great character", but he aimed sharp ‌criticism at referee Miguel Angel Ortiz Arias and those who appointed him.

"They've put a referee, aged 41, with no international experience - it's certainly not because he's a great referee," Mourinho said.

"Then the poor chap has come ‌here and hasn't been able to cope with the pressure - and it really is intense pressure. I call it '80s-style pressure' here in this stadium, which you hardly ever see these days."

Asked about being six points behind Barcelona, Mourinho offered a pointed reply.

"If they just leave us in peace and let us compete on a level playing field ⁠with everyone else, we've still got a long way to go," he said.

"I don't ​want to go so far as to say this was set up... I ​want to believe that they simply made a mistake."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Former Spurs captain Cristian Romero avoided a red card in the Madrid derby after making this challenge on Jude Bellingham

'A derby marked by poor officiating,' say Real Madrid

Real Madrid also released an official match report after full-time which echoed the views of Mourinho.

The La Liga club claimed the defeat was "marked by poor officiating".

"Real Madrid lost at the Metropolitano in a derby marked by the poor officiating of Ortiz Arias, who failed to send off Cuti Romero in the first half for stepping on Jude Bellingham's knee (despite reviewing the play on the monitor) and Kang-In Lee for stepping on Valverde's left ankle.

"Both decisions shaped the match, which was decided in the second half in favor of Atletico.

"Until the 30th minute, the game had very few dangerous plays. But from that point on, controversy took over the derby.

"In the 35th minute, during a contested ball, Bellingham got to the ball before Cuti Romero, and the Atletico defender planted his studs into the left knee of the Madrid player. Ortiz Arias initially booked our player but was called by Trujillo Suarez to review the incident on the monitor.

"After watching the replay, he rescinded the card from Bellingham and issued a yellow card to the Atletico defender instead of sending him off.

"Nine minutes later, the referee made another crucial error by not penalizing Kang-In Lee for a challenge on Valverde, where he struck him with his studs on the left ankle.

"Ortiz Arias was close to the incident but did not show a red card (or even a yellow card) to the Atlético player, nor was he alerted by Trujillo Suárez on this occasion."

Sports.title: Cutler beat one McKenna, now he wants world champ brother
Sports.content:
Lee Cutler beat one McKenna brother, now he wants to fight the other for the world middleweight title.

Cutler overcame Stevie McKenna in a thriller in 2024. He lost a technical decision to Sam Eggington in another exciting match-up. Now looking to roar back to form, Cutler stopped Aaron Sutton in a Bournemouth homecoming and will take on Louis Greene next.

Greene, a hard puncher, has a tremendous aggressive style of fighting too. Cutler and Greene will collide at the Copper Box Arena on Saturday, live on Sky Sports.

"It's a dangerous fight," Cutler told Sky Sports. "I don't say no. It's a fight that the fans want to see and it's fight that I believe takes me to another level.

"[Greene is] tough. Punches extremely hard. I've got to be switched on for the full 10 rounds that we're in there. I'm fully prepared for a hard night.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Louis Greene is predicting fireworks in his bout against Lee Cutler on Zuffa Boxing 11.

"It's one of those fights, we're a stepping stone for each other and that's how we've got to see each other," he added.

"I've got to be smart in there and box how I know I can box. If I can do that I'll come away with the victory."

He had been expecting Stevie McKenna to look for a rematch with him.

McKenna levelled Owen O'Neill on the undercard of brother Aaron McKenna's IBF middleweight world title victory.

"It does surprise me. I thought I was going to get a callout after. I thought he might not want to fight me on the Dublin card because it's a big night for the family because of the brother and stuff," Cutler reflected.

"But I was fully expecting him to get through his opponent and then call me out after that. But the fact he didn't even mention my name, goes to show what he's about."

If he can get through his middleweight 10 rounder with Greene he will look for an eventual fight with new champion Aaron McKenna.

"I think he's very good. I think he's a tough fight for anyone. But he's somebody that I see myself in there with. Bring him on," Cutler declared.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Stephen McKenna and Lee Cutler exchanged a pair of verbal jabs after their respective Zuffa Boxing 07 wins in Bournemouth.

"But as I said I'm focusing fully on Louis Green because he's a very dangerous opponent and if I take my eye off the ball for one second, anything can happen.

"I'm a come forward fighter, he's a come forward fighter, he's a huge puncher, very dangerous.

"All he has to do is touch somebody and then it's lights out."

Sports.title: Spurs bottom of PL but more than £300m spent - where do they go from here?
Sports.content:
This time it was supposed to be different. After multiple false dawns for Tottenham Hotspur, the club had a manager with proven Premier League experience, and had handed him a £300m+ war chest - easily the biggest in its entire history.

Instead, Spurs find themselves bottom of the table after five games for the first time in 18 years, with their only goals a pair of consolation strikes on another dismal afternoon against Aston Villa at the weekend.

Things aren't quite as bad as the table suggests and had Tottenham taken any of a number of presentable first-half chances against Villa, they would have gone into the three-week international break silencing some of the noise around the club.

But instead, two points from five games and such a dismal record in front of goal has kept the spotlight firmly on them.

Though it is only five games, their struggles to find consistency have extended into a third consecutive season. Tottenham have now picked up just 18 points in 2026 and, since the start of 2024/25, still one fewer than a West Ham side who were relegated at the end of last season.

Roberto De Zerbi cannot avoid scrutiny forever, especially after a summer where he was given relative carte blanche in the transfer market and, a top-class left-winger aside, got most of what he asked for.

Speaking before the Villa game, he hinted he would have liked to have done things differently during the summer window, but the club had to respect Financial Fair Play and some players who had been earmarked for sale remained at the club.

That will not afford him much sympathy given the size of Spurs' spend. One of the outgoings who they were happy to let go, Luka Vuskovic, is thriving at Brighton. Meanwhile, the player he replaced, Jan Paul van Hecke, toiled in that Villa defeat and was dribbled past three times.

Regardless, Tottenham were always unlikely to be an overnight fix given money alone will not solve the sizeable task of changing course after finishing 17th in back-to-back seasons.

Spurs' big summer of spending Sandro Tonali - Newcastle, £100m

Savio - Man City, £85m

But fans still expected something more than this, especially from a head coach known for his man-management and getting the best out of limited resources, as he demonstrated across nearly two years on the south coast at Brighton.

Even one win would lift them out of the quagmire - and they will target a similarly under-pressure Man Utd side when the Premier League returns on October 10, live on Sky Sports. However, there are a number of issues of concern even after that mammoth spend.

The naive manner Spurs fell behind to Villa with Micky Van de Ven off the pitch injured and Andy Robertson inadvertently teeing up the opportunity, led De Zerbi to complain that "leaders have to be leaders" in such crunch moments. "We can't lose games in this way," he added.

But does his squad have enough of that kind of player? Van de Ven, Pedro Porro, Ben Davies, James Maddison and Archie Gray were named as De Zerbi's five-man leadership group last month, but none would be considered an out-and-out natural leader, who can hoist his team-mates up by their collars.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch highlights of Spurs' 3-2 defeat at Aston Villa which saw them go into the first international break bottom of the Premier League table

This is nothing new. Despite long-standing allegations of being 'Spursy', in the last two years, that nickname has truly taken on a new form. Tottenham have not won a league game when conceding first in approaching two years and have picked up only nine draws from losing positions since.

It was the right time for Cristian Romero to move on in the summer largely because his aggression could often overstep the mark, but it has left a void which has not been filled.

Instead, it has been compounded by the further loss of perhaps limited but unquestionably combative midfielder Joao Palhinha. In De Zerbi's defence, he made no secret of his desire to keep him.

More worryingly, it does not appear a problem the head coach has a solution to. "It is difficult to explain," he admitted after Saturday's defeat. "In my 14 years as a coach, I've never seen a team like us, so fragile and inconsistent."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Even ahead of Saturday's defeat to Aston Villa, Roberto De Zerbi explained the reasons behind Spurs' dismal start and highlights where they need to improve

He need only look to the home stands if he needs any filling in from a fanbase who are all too used to seeing exactly that over the past two years.

Even without Palhinha he cannot complain too loudly about his midfield given the near £200m sanctioned to sign Sandro Tonali and Matheus Fernandes.

Tonali in particular should be fresh after a summer off from the World Cup, but has yet to hit the heights which made him a fan favourite for much of his time at Newcastle and convinced Spurs to break their transfer record to sign him.

The bizarre sideshow of Richarlison's future has not helped matters either, despite his own limitations. That too is only compounded by Spurs' lack of goals while last season's top scorer watches on from his own, albeit partly self-imposed, spell in exile.

Dominic Solanke has still not returned to full fitness and De Zerbi was almost apologetic for his out-of-form striker after his latest performance against Villa, saying "he's much better than this Dominic Solanke".

But with the average xG of Spurs' shots the lowest across the Premier League and their overall total better only than Coventry's, the real Solanke needs to stand up sooner rather than later - or Omar Marmoush re-find his scoring boots.

It is still very early days in the latest iteration of the Spurs machine, and given the significant turnover in players in the summer - over half of Saturday's starting line-up were not at the club last season - no surprise there have been some teething problems.

But the sight of a Premier League table showing two points, two goals and Spurs holding up the rest of the league will feel like a lot more than that.

There is still a feeling things will come good - there is undoubted quality in the squad and no-one needs reminding of De Zerbi's abilities. But his spells elsewhere have a habit of ending on a sour note. The hope is that it hasn't already set in here.

Sports.title: Come back soon Premier League, the endlessly moreish mega-product | Barney Ronay
Sports.content:
Get ready for the dopamine crash. And this one really is a proper autumn nosedive. The past 17 days up to and including Sunday’s cut-off gave us 30 Premier League games and 79 goals. Which, if you take Spurs out of it – and this is fair because Spurs are now post‑goal, an entertainment concept unrelated to goals or even football itself – is really quite a lot.

Are your pathways stimulated? Are the neural connectors flickering? Well get ready for cold turkey, for 19 blank days of shivers and shakes until the Premier League show resumes in October. Maybe it really is time to buy one of those powders off the internet.

The international break will provide its own intrigue. There will be discussions about whether Thomas Tuchel is or isn’t responsible for the inherited cultural weaknesses of English football. There will be rage at Tuchel’s inability to coach the players to keep the ball as never before via his few short hours on the training pitch. And yet more rage at the real issues, basically the fact he continues to be German and looks like a scurvy-ridden Napoleonic naval commander powered solely by ship’s biscuits and morphine.

This is unlikely to fill the hole. There will be an unavoidable “contrast effect”, the rush of adrenaline that only serves to deepen the low when it is gone. But there are also some familiar autumn rituals to help us through. One of these is the state‑of‑the‑nation Premier League address, pegged out around key questions such as “where are we?”, “what are we?” and “where is it all going?”. This time around these are relatively easy to answer.

Five rounds into the Premier League season this is pretty much a cut-and-paste job. The big news: there is no big news. Events continue to happen at great volume. But in terms of teams, style, stars, energies and potential outcomes, not much has changed. Roll back one year and this was the broad situation. A powerful team with a bald, irascible manager had won all five games, but also looked defensively fragile. The team that would win the league was second. That team was also Arsenal.

View image in fullscreen Are Tottenham doomed? Probably not. They have enough semi-interested players to retain a solid hold on 17th place. Photograph: News Images/NurPhoto/Shutterstock

The middle classes were the most interesting story, those functional, well-run teams beginning with B, an entity you might call Brightonmouth. Erling Haaland was scoring goals. Bruno Fernandes was generating hair‑tearing anguish, like a young Elvis, but based more around shithousery and risky attacking passes.

As ever there are still some key questions doing the rounds, but luckily these can all be answered easily. Is Michael Carrick the man to take Manchester United to the next level? No. Is Michael Carrick the reason United are not at that level, but in a state where they must now employ Michael Carrick? Also no.

The reality for United is that there are no other levels. This is the level, a club that instead acts as a grand, angst-ridden but very accurate metaphor for modern‑day Britain, furiously retailing its own heritage, run by fill-ins and opportunists, a mobile waxwork museum living on tourism and memories.

Are Tottenham doomed? Probably not. They have enough semi-interested players to retain a solid hold on 17th place. Although frustratingly for Premier League content addicts, even this has been degraded by repetition. Spurs could get relegated now and you would just keep scrolling.

Are Liverpool on the verge of a renaissance? Probably not. The Jürgen Klopp golden era is beginning to look quite distant, surrounded on all sides by something a bit like the present. And, yes, Florian Wirtz is a very good footballer. He just can’t resist contact very well, which is non‑negotiable in the Premier League. He is going to be really good at Paris Saint-Gemain/Bayern Munich/Inter.

View image in fullscreen Manchester United have had a difficult start to the season under Michael Carrick. Photograph: Dennis Goodwin/ProSports/Shutterstock

Otherwise, it is a case of stasis and a reliable, entertaining, homogenised product. Tactically, we can still get excited about small changes. If you analyse it deeply you may find a little more counterattack, Anthony Elanga running fast, an inverted winger discovering almost by accident he can also cross with his strong foot.

It is a mark of how standardised the game has become that these are deemed things worth getting excited about. There is still only one elite level style, the Omniball template of the Cruyff-Michels-Guardiola-Gegenpressing school.
