In the last week academy starlet JJ Gabriel, nicknamed 'Kid Messi', has requested to leave the club due to his family's view that it has fallen behind the heavyweights of European football.

Daily Mail Sport has reported that a source close to the family explained that United are 'far away' from the likes of Barcelona, Real Madrid, Bayern Munich as well as domestic rivals Arsenal and Manchester City, and that they want him to 'learn from the best' to maximise his talents.

Away from the pitch, Ratcliffe has been much-maligned for mass staff redundancies as well as increasing match ticket prices and season-ticket relocations in order to accommodate further hospitality seating. Ratcliffe also plans to build a new 100,000-seater stadium.

Fans protested against United's ownership ahead of and during September's Manchester derby defeat, and supporters' groups have called on Ratcliffe to resign over his recent comments on immigration.

Lineker added: 'It is a bit of a mess, that club. You've got a ground that's falling apart, all sorts of complaints about various things.

He congratulated the unpopular Glazers on finding Ratcliffe - 'someone even worse than them'

Talented youngster JJ Gabriel, nicknamed 'Kid Messi', has requested to leave the club due to his family's view that it has fallen behind the heavyweights of European football

'They're losing young teenagers, it looks like that (Gabriel leaving) is going to happen.

'The results, the inconsistency seems to be back. They have backed the manager many times and it’s not worked for them but there’s got to be something dripping down from the top.'

Previously, Ratcliffe has said that excessive criticism would cause him to walk away from the club if he was 'abused' by fans in the same way the Glazer family have.

The unpopular Glazer family bought the club in 2005 via a leveraged takeover and retain a majority stake.

'I mean, I can put up with it for a while,' Ratcliffe said in March. 'I don't mind being unpopular because I get that nobody likes seeing Manchester United down where they are, and nobody likes the decisions we're having to make at the moment.

'If I draw a bit of the ire, I can put up with that. But I'm no different to the average person. It's not nice, particularly for friends and family.

'So, eventually, if it reached the extent that the Glazer family have been abused, then I'd have to say, look, enough's enough guys, let somebody else do this.

'They can't really come to a match, the Glazers. They've retreated into the shadows a bit now, so I'm getting all the stick.'

Sports.title: Tottenham plunged deeper into the mire as relegation chances soar, while Arsenal and Man City pull clear in two-horse title race: Supercomputer's updated Premier League predictions after five games
Sports.content:
Tottenham plunged deeper into the mire as relegation chances soar, while Arsenal and Man City pull clear in two-horse title race: Supercomputer's updated Premier League predictions after five games

The international break is here, giving Premier League clubs time to take stock of what has been a thrilling start to the 2026-27 season, and Opta to reevaluate their title predictions for the season's close.

We're only five games in and there are already a number of intriguing storylines developing, not least so-called relegation favourites Hull City's rampant return to the top flight after nine years away, claiming eight points to sit eighth heading into the break.

Enzo Maresca's start to life in charge of Manchester City couldn't have gone any better, winning all five games to clinch top spot as the only team with a 100 per cent record.

Brighton's stunning 3-0 defeat of Arsenal at the weekend has left the Premier League champions in second, while Fabian Hurzeler's side are next in line in third.

Only goal difference separates fourth to seventh in Brentford, Leeds, Liverpool and Everton, who each remain unbeaten so far.

Meanwhile, Chelsea are 10th with seven points, Michael Carrick's Manchester United are 12th and Tottenham, despite spending around £302million this summer, sit bottom of the table after collecting just two points. With Opta now giving them a 30 per cent chance of relegation, the outlook is already looking bleak for Roberto De Zerbi's side.

City's chances to win the title have increased considerably, closing the gap on Arsenal to 39.8 per cent, with Opta essentially predicting a two-horse race

To recap, Opta's supercomputer gave Arsenal a 40.6 per cent chance of retaining their title at the start of the campaign, making them favourites.

Manchester City were comfortably second favourites at 19.6 per cent, followed by Liverpool with 9.2 per cent and Manchester United with 6.6 per cent.

Interestingly, despite suffering that heavy defeat to the Seagulls at the weekend, Arsenal remain Opta's favourites to lift the trophy at the end of the season, with that percentage increasing to 43.7 per cent.

At the same time, City's chances have also increased considerably, closing the gap on Arsenal to 39.8 per cent, with Opta essentially predicting a two-horse race.

Liverpool are third favourites, but only with 5.7 per cent, that figure dropping slightly from the start of the season.

Brighton are now fourth favourites with 4.2 per cent. Brentford are fifth (1.2 per cent), Everton sixth (1.1 per cent) and Chelsea seventh (1.0 per cent).

Man United have struggled to put points on the board so far despite leading the Premier League for total shots (113) and touches in the opposition box (182). They have, as a result, fallen from fourth favourites at the beginning of the season to eighth, having just a 0.9 per cent chance of winning the title, the biggest fall of any team.

Aston Villa picked up their first win of the season against rock-bottom Spurs but lost three of their opening four matches and have been given just a 0.7 per cent chance of winning the title.

Join the discussion Should Spurs fans be furious about their club’s dramatic decline despite massive transfer spending?

Opta are giving Spurs a 30 per cent chance of relegation after their poor start to the season

And despite getting off to a strong start, Xabi Alonso's Chelsea side have now gone three games without a win and are given a 0.95 per cent chance of winning the title.

At the other end of the table, Coventry City, despite winning their first game of the season against Nottingham Forest at the weekend, are favourites to go down, with Opta giving them a 45.1 per cent chance of relegation.

Next in line for the drop are Alvaro Arbeloa's Fulham, who have a 42.4 per cent chance of relegation.

And finally, Roberto De Zerbi's Tottenham are third favourites to fall into the Championship at the end of the season, with the supercomputer having given them a 30 per cent chance of relegation.

Sports.title: Mo Salah handed six-month driving ban for speeding in his Rolls-Royce - just days after revealing his emotional Liverpool departure
Sports.content:
Former Liverpool footballer Mohamed Salah has been banned from driving for six months after his Rolls-Royce was clocked speeding.

The player failed to tell police who was at the wheel when the car was caught by a speed camera driving at 36mph on a 30mph stretch of road in Wilmslow, Cheshire, on March 27, according to court documents.

The 34-year-old did not respond to the notice of the prosecution, brought by Cheshire Constabulary, and did not enter a plea to the charge.

A court official said he was prosecuted at Warrington Combined Court under the Single Justice Procedure, which sees magistrates sit in private hearings, and was convicted of failing to give information relating to the identification of the driver of the Rolls Royce.

Salah has been banned from driving for six months after his Rolls-Royce was clocked speeding

The Egypt national captain was handed a six-month driving ban and ordered to pay £1,044, the court spokeswoman said.

The speeding offence came days after Salah announced he would be leaving Liverpool following nine years with the team.

Announcing his departure on March 24, the club said he had 'firmly established himself as one of the greatest players in Liverpool’s history'.

He scored 257 goals in 442 appearances for Liverpool, before transferring to Turkish side Trabzonspor following the 2025-26 season.

Sports.title: Paul Scholes accuses Man United of 'a lack of ambition' and 'buying players for the sake of it' - rather than trying to win the Premier League - and claims Michael Carrick will feel 'let down' by his bosses
Sports.content:
Paul Scholes accuses Man United of 'a lack of ambition' and 'buying players for the sake of it' - rather than trying to win the Premier League - and claims Michael Carrick will feel 'let down' by his bosses

Paul Scholes has claimed that Michael Carrick has been let down by the Manchester United hierarchy with their 'lack of ambition' over the summer.

United have managed to win just one of their opening five games of the season, a 5-2 victory over promoted side Ipswich Town. Otherwise, they have lost to Hull City and Manchester City, and have drawn against Everton and Fulham. They have also been knocked out of the Carabao Cup at the first time of asking.

United had a modest summer in the transfer market. With Casemiro leaving for Inter Miami and Manuel Ugarte - now injured - deemed not good enough, Elliot Anderson and Mateus Fernandes emerged as Carrick's top midfield targets. But Anderson joined Man City from Nottingham Forest in a £116million deal, while Fernandes chose Tottenham over United for £85m.

The club also considered Sandro Tonali and Bruno Guimaraes, but baulked at the fees required to sign the pair, who eventually joined Spurs (£92.5m) and Arsenal (£75m) respectively.

Instead, United signed Carlos Baleba for £70million, though the Cameroon international is yet to feature after arriving with an ankle injury. Andrey Santos joined for £48m but has started only once, while Youri Tielemans arrived for £35m and Karl Darlow on a free transfer.

Carrick also wanted a new left back, but the club failed to provide cover or a long-term successor for the 31-year-old Luke Shaw.

Scholes has claimed that Carrick has been let down by the Manchester United hierarchy with their 'lack of ambition' over the summer

United have managed to win just one of their opening five games of the season, a 5-2 victory over promoted side Ipswich Town and have lost to Hull City and Manchester City

United legend Scholes has voiced his concern over the situation, with the club sitting in 12th after five games.

'It feels quite sad to say this but Man United are a club now that are not trying to win the league with recruitment,' he said on The Good, The Bat & The Football podcast.

'Santos, Baleba, they've brought players in that physically they may be better. Santos played 11 games for Chelsea, they paid £50million for him.

'But he's not getting into the team, now Baleba might make a bit of difference. But again, if you're recruiting at the start of the season for Manchester United, it should be for players that you think you can go and win the league with. I think they're a million miles away.

'I think they're just trying to consolidate from what Michael did last year, which is hard to get your head around. Were United trying to buy an Elliot Anderson? Probably. Now that's a signing where you think that might help you get a lot better. The players they've bought aren't making them any better.'

Centre-forward appears to be a particular sticking point for Scholes and his podcast partner Nicky Butt. United appeared willing to let forward Joshua Zirkzee leave the club in the summer, although a move failed to materialise.

Carrick has remained reluctant to play the Dutchman in Benjamin Sesko's absence and he has made just two substitute appearances in the Premier League so far, with Matheus Cunha getting the nod up top instead.

Butt said: 'Playing Cunha as a nine - it kills him, he's not a nine. He's nowhere near the player he is when he's playing off the side. We haven't got a number nine other than (Benjamin) Sesko. Zirkzee doesn't look anywhere near a Man United number nine. How can Man United have one centre forward that they can rely on?'

Carrick has been reluctant to play Zirkzee in Benjamin Sesko's absence and he has made just two substitute appearances in the Premier League

Carrick guided United to third in the Premier League last season, and both Scholes and Butt have claimed that Carrick has been let down by the club's hierarchy.

Scholes said: 'Michael must be really disappointed with what has happened in the summer. I reckon behind the scenes he thinks he's been let down. What Michael did last year was very, very good.

'The most important time for Michael was the start of this season. These games now are where you put a marker down, it gives you a foundation for the rest of the season.'

United have already seen two managers depart since Sir Jim Ratcliffe's INEOS took over footballing operations in February 2024. Erik ten Hag was sacked three months after being handed a new deal in October 2024. His replacement, Ruben Amorim, was then sacked in January this year after 14 months in charge.

Butt said: 'As a fan, the bit that gets me, I no longer think "it's a no-brainer we're going to win this game". Who can you point the finger at, and for me, it has to be the people upstairs that are pointing the people into place to pick the managers, the players, the coaches.

'I don't understand it. (Omar) Berrada the CEO said they're going to win the league by 2028. That's never going to happen the way it's going, never in a million years.

'I don't understand it. (Omar) Berrada the CEO said they're going to win the league by 2028. That's never going to happen the way it's going, never in a million years,' Butt said

'Without literally ripping them to shreds, it has to be said they've come in, they gave Ten Hag an extra few years on his contract, that didn't work. They went and got two other managers after that and it's still not working.

'There's got to be a real question being asked - is it being run right off the pitch, in recruitment and then that translates onto the pitch. So it's a massive big problem I think.'

Scholes added: 'I don't think we can keep blaming managers all the time. You can't just keep going through managers like we are doing. Recruitment will have an awful lot to answer for, especially after this summer.

'Are they looking at these top targets, Morgan Rogers, Elliot Anderson? It feels like we're buying players just for the sake of it. It feels like they're settling for third, fourth, fifth-best signings - and that isn't good enough. I'd rather just keep the money, and say "sure we can find someone in the academy who can do what these lads are doing".'

Sports.title: Brighton's demolition of Arsenal dissected: The Seagulls' power press, Bart Verbruggen's clever tactic, exploiting Mikel Arteta's new idea and preying on David Raya's weakness
Sports.content:
So much, then, for Arsenal’s uncontested stroll to a second Premier League title under Mikel Arteta. So much for the idea that this impenetrable fortress would remain unconquered all season, for who could possibly possess the weapons with which to breach it. Brighton have quickly put paid to that. ‘There was only one team who tried to play football today,’ was Fabian Hurzeler’s pointed remark after the Gunners clung on to a 1-0 lead at the Amex Stadium back in March. Six months later, it was the Brighton boss who provided Arteta with his own brutal lesson of how to do so and one, perhaps, that Arsenal’s rivals could look to follow on their quest to dethrone them. PRESS, PRESS, PRESS The biggest of Brighton’s weapons was their relentless press. From the first minute until the last, the Seagulls swarmed around Arsenal, man-to-man, as high and as wide up the pitch as possible. It was in complete contrast to the trick used by Manchester City last season under Pep Guardiola where their front four would sit off the Arsenal backline, refuse to press them, and instead cut off the passing lanes into midfield. Brighton wanted to harass Arsenal so much that they either won possession high up the pitch – the Seagulls won the ball back 10 times in the final third, the most of any team this season, and the last side to do so more often against Arsenal was Liverpool in April 2023 – or panic them into dangerous passes into midfield where they would be waiting. Brighton allowed Arsenal no time to settle on the ball at the Amex Stadium on Saturday as they ran out 3-0 winners Brighton won possession from Arsenal 10 times in the final third of the pitch These two examples (below) came from inside the first five minutes. On one occasion in between, Arsenal keeper David Raya was so flummoxed he passed the ball straight out for a throw in. Brighton crowd the Arsenal players high up the pitch and win the ball back Again, Brighton's press has Arsenal in all sorts of trouble in their box with nowhere to go The key was Brighton just didn’t stop. It’s all well and good harrying and hustling and chasing down all over the pitch from the first minute but, eventually, you tire and you fade and don’t jump up as quickly or aggressively as you did at the start. Only Brighton didn’t. They kept going. Even at 3-0 up, with nearly an hour gone, they swarm around Arsenal’s players to create another chance. The Seagulls push up and force Ezri Konsa to play a pass into midfield towards Bukayo Saka only for Brighton to nick it back, burst into the area and Charalampos Kostoulas goes down in the box looking for a penalty. Ezri Konsa plays the ball into midfield to try to find Bukayo Saka... ...but Saka is immediately under pressure and Brighton win the ball back Just a minute later, Arsenal get the ball back on the other side of the pitch. By the time Bruno Guimaraes receives the pass, he is surrounded by four blue shirts with nowhere to go. Brighton keep the Gunners where they want them. Bruno Guimaraes is swamped by Brighton players and can find no way out That came, as it happens, from Brighton lumping the ball upfield from just outside their own box and out for a throw-in. This, too, was a key aspect of their play. GO LONG, CAUSE CHAOS We’ve seen it with other high-pressing teams like Bournemouth when they lump the ball, rugby-style, into touch from the kick-off because they would rather try to win the ball back as close to the opposition goal as possible. Brighton did it frequently, in open play, and often via goalkeeper Bart Verbruggen. For Brighton’s first goal, the Seagulls had a throw-in deep in the final third, almost level with the edge of Arsenal’s box, but still they eventually worked the ball all the way back to Verbruggen, who stood with his studs on the ball while the centre backs split and, eventually, went long to the right. After some neat passing, the ball found Pascal Gross, who fired in from range. The Brighton keeper frequently targeted that side, as you can see from his pass map (below). The feeling was that even if the usually physically dominant Arsenal side won the first ball, the Seagulls would be there to flock around the second. The map shows Bart Verbruggen using the long ball a lot and frequently favouring Arsenal's left-back position Right back Ferdi Kadioglu pushed up high down that side to frequently box Arsenal in. A look at their average position maps, too, shows just how Brighton locked down that side of the pitch. The average position of Brighton players in their victory over Arsenal and how they doubled up on their right wing EXPLOITING ARTETA’S EVOLUTION It was not all about the press for Brighton, though. Whenever Arsenal did get on the ball inside the Seagulls’ half, the hosts dropped into a deep, deep block. They either wanted to win the ball close to Arsenal’s box, or near their own - and spring a counter. Look here (below), how Brighton have all 11 players behind the ball as Arsenal look to find a way through just before the hour. Brighton are back in shape with all their players behind the ball as Arsenal try in vain to find a way through Brighton eventually win possession back just outside their box and break. Not even a minute later, after pressing to win the ball back high up the pitch, they win the corner from which they score their third goal. Brighton’s four ‘fast breaks’, Opta’s phrase for a counter attack, and their three shots that came from them, were their most in a Premier League game since 2019. The last time Arsenal faced more in a match was 2018. Hurzeler was exploiting Arteta’s changing style. For so long, the complaint about Arsenal is how they were so obsessed with control that they never took enough risks to create enough in open play. That appears, maybe, to be changing. After just four matches this season, Arsenal have attempted the third most fast breaks themselves with 10. This is a change. Last season they were ranked ninth. The season before that 12th and, two seasons before that, 16th with just 18 all campaign. It adds an extra dimension to their play but they are yet to find the balance and, as Brighton showed, you can hurt them in transition. Their second goal comes straight from an Arsenal counter attack, where Saka fluffs a shot straight into Verbruggen’s hands, and Brighton spring one of their own. TEST RAYA FROM RANGE Brighton’s first two goals came from shots from outside the box. So was the one Arsenal conceded against Chelsea, the only other league match in which they have been breached. Seven of the last 18 Premier League goals Arsenal have conceded have come from distance. Is this becoming a weakness? A stat from Opta did the rounds after the match stating that among goalkeepers that have conceded at least 100 Premier League goals only Hans Segers (22 per cent) has conceded a higher percentage from outside the penalty area than David Raya (20.6 per cent).

Your browser does not support iframes.

Arsenal's David Raya was beaten from distance again during the defeat at Brighton It is slightly unfair to pick him out as Arsenal’s defence is so good that teams are often reduced to having to shoot from miles away but of the 22 goalkeepers to start at least 40 league matches since the start of the 2023-24 season, when Raya joined the Gunners, only two have a worse save percentage from outside the box (Raya's is 78 per cent). You can bet that teams, even if they aren’t already, will start to pepper Raya’s goal from range now. HAVE THEY BEEN FOUND OUT? Is this the key, then, to beating this unbeatable Arsenal? Well, for a start, Brighton’s approach was exceptionally high risk with so many bodies committed to press so high. Arsenal had plenty of chances, including Kai Havertz missing a one-on-one. Few teams, too, have the energy, physicality and tactical discipline to pull it off for 90 minutes like Brighton did. Not every long-range shot, too, will nestle in the bottom corner, let alone two. However, the manner of the defeat, the lack of balance and control, has certainly given Arteta three weeks to think about what went wrong. The Gunners still boast one of the best defences in world football but Brighton have proved they are not quite so untouchable after all.

Sports.title: How Gary Neville is missing the point over Man United's running stats, why Michael Carrick isn't worried about 'lack of effort', the way he's copying Sir Alex Ferguson and the numbers that tell the other side of the story
Sports.content:
How Gary Neville is missing the point over Man United's running stats, why Michael Carrick isn't worried about 'lack of effort', the way he's copying Sir Alex Ferguson and the numbers that tell the other side of the story

The truth is, Michael Carrick made his feelings clear on running statistics long before fronting up at Fulham on Sunday night.

Where others such as Gary Neville are apoplectic with rage at the lethargy ('lack of effort' as Neville put it) with which Manchester United are playing – he described a spell in the first half as the worst 15 minutes he had seen from United in 45 years – Carrick is not.

He didn’t focus on running stats as a player, and certainly doesn’t now.

‘David [Moyes] was right that in terms of “distance covered” we weren’t one of the top sides in the Premier League,’ Carrick wrote in his 2018 book Between the Lines, recalling one of Moyes’ first meetings with the squad upon succeeding Sir Alex Ferguson, in which he vowed to have them running more.

‘But if you look back over the years, all the good years, teams might come to Old Trafford and run a lot more than us, but quite often we ended up winning 2-0, 3-0 or 4-0. Under Sir Alex, we were very efficient with the ball.’

At Middlesbrough, though, ask their supporters what the biggest weakness of Carrick’s Boro side was and they will unanimously cite the lack of intensity in the press and the defensive issues that arose because of it.

Gary Neville was fuming at United's lack of effort in their 1-1 draw with Fulham at the weekend

Then he had Jonny Howson and Hayden Hackney as a midfield pair, now it’s Kobbie Mainoo and Youri Tielemans. On the ball both pairs are brilliant. Without it, the shortcomings are strikingly similar.

The thing is, win games and nobody talks about running stats. Win the game and the number of minutes spent at high intensity is likely airbrushed from the conversation. Win the game and the pros and cons of your system and your beliefs are saved for another day.

But United aren’t winning. They lost at Hull City in abject fashion. They lost to the 10 men of Manchester City. They drew at Everton and they drew at Fulham.

Even with a 5-2 win against Ipswich Town, this is United’s worst start to a Premier League season since 2013-14. Fail to beat Tottenham Hotspur and Carrick will officially have masterminded United’s worst ever start to a Premier League campaign.

Fundamentally there is a chasm between a fanbase that want to see intensity, a buzzword that has stalked United for years, and effort, versus a manager that believes distance covered, sprints made and sheer physical output is not the only way to win a football match.

So, you end up here, United heading into the international break dead last in sprints made, dead last in distance covered at high intensity, dead last in the amount of time spent at high intensity, dead last in the amount of time sprinting, and with only three teams spending more time walking without the ball than United do. And with a manager who rejects all criticism about those metrics.

‘I didn't think we did [look passive]. Did you think we were passive? Football is a difficult game,’ Carrick said as the inquest into the drab Fulham draw began with haste.

‘We controlled a lot of the first half and we played a lot of good football today. There are going to be spells when you don't have it go your own way.

Youri Tielemans is brilliant on the ball for United but without it his shortcomings are there for all to see

Michael Carrick refuses to get hung up on Manchester United's running statistics

'To expect total dominance for the whole game, I don't think anyone gets that in this league.’

Passivity has been a trigger word for Carrick all season long. He rejected that assessment at Hull, and did so again at Everton and now at Fulham. Where he sees control and patience, others see laziness and a lack of ideas.

To indulge Carrick, let’s look beyond the surface numbers that went viral soon after the final whistle. What we know to be true is that United ran 6.5 kilometres less than Fulham on the day, the second biggest disparity between teams when 11 v 11 so far this season.

What we also know to be true is that Fulham started their passing sequences – when moves in attack begin – 36.9 metres from Senne Lammens’ goal, on average. In this latest round of matches, no side started closer to their opponents' goal than Fulham did.

We also know that Bryan Mbeumo was the only United player to sprint more than 305 yards against Fulham, with 408.4. Bruno Fernandes, for example, was recorded to have sprinted just 35.2 yards in total. Kobbie Mainoo clocked in at 71.5 yards.

It can also be pointed out that of the top 70 players in the league this season for number of sprints made, only two play for United in Mbeumo and Marcus Rashford. Brentford and Bournemouth combine for 11 players in this category.

But then you need to look at the numbers Carrick cares about. The numbers he is focusing on. Numbers that show United had 29 shots against Fulham, taking their overall total to 113, ranking first of all 20 Premier League sides.

Or the fact that Carrick’s side rank third in the league for expected goals (xG), with 9.9. Or the fact they rank first in the league for touches in the opposition’s box (182) and have allowed the fewest touches in their own penalty area (92). They are fourth in the league for possession and second in the league for most accurate passes per match.

All of the above statistics point to the conclusion that this so-called 'lethargic' United has to be, in part, by design.

No, Carrick will not be explicitly telling players not to run and not to work hard, no manager would. Yet he fundamentally disagrees that those metrics represent the keys to success.

Liverpool, for example, are the side which cover the least ground in the league under Andoni Iraola, yet they also top the sprint charts. It doesn’t have to be one or the other, that’s the gripe among United fans.

Carrick wants to evolve into a possession-focused, pass-dominant side that can manage matches at their own pace, strangling the life out of teams through control. His own style as a player, going back to his dismissal of Moyes in his book, has unquestionably influenced his ideology.

‘Naturally, we all see the game for certain things,' Carrick explained to reporters at a sit-down during pre-season. 'We enjoy seeing different things and your eye naturally takes you to different parts of the game. We can all watch the game and see something a little bit different.

‘Just being a midfielder, that's how I've seen the game. In some ways, it helps because you kind of connected to all parts of the team over time.

‘I'm not saying you have to be a midfielder to be a good coach, but I think it's just how my reference points are in some ways and what I feel's worked over the years, what kind of football I think the supporters want to see as well, and hopefully that fits together.’

Supporters want to see wins but they crucially want to see effort and application upon the eye test, regardless of the more detailed data.

Bruno Fernandes sprinted for just 35.2 yards at Craven Cottage on Sunday

Calvin Bassey celebrates United's own goal that put Fulham ahead

‘It's about intensity, body language, physicality,' Ralf Rangnick explained in December 2021. 'This was always the case. If you want to keep control of a game like this you need to be physically present, and this wasn't the case in all positions.'

‘I think the main problem, that we did before in games much better, is intensity,' Erik ten Hag mused in October 2022. 'We have to bring the intensity in every game on the pitch. That was the big difference between City and us.'

‘Most important is the intensity,' Ruben Amorim bluntly pointed out in December last year. 'You can feel it right away, when we start the game. We can feel when we are at the top level in intensity and when we are not, and you cannot win games in this way.’

All that sounds and feels painfully familiar.

Fans believe intensity holds the key, as does Matheus Cunha, who spoke passionately about it after the Fulham game. Three of Carrick’s predecessors believe success is built on the foundation of intensity, while director of football Jason Wilcox previously talked up the ‘intensity’ in training sessions day in, day out.

But if you have a head coach whose philosophy goes against everything the Premier League has become in terms of blood and thunder football played in fast forward, is a three-week break really going to deliver the change required? Doubtful.

Carrick is determined to do it his way and that’s why United are never going to be the Duracell bunnies of the Premier League under his watch.

This feels like a hill that Carrick is very much willing to die on.

Sports.title: Florian Wirtz must prove Jurgen Klopp right as Liverpool sent 'last hope' warning
Sports.content:
Florian Wirtz must prove Jurgen Klopp right as Liverpool sent 'last hope' warning

Florian Wirtz still isn't firing for Liverpool and came in for criticism following their 1-0 win at Bournemouth - but he can expect an arm around the shoulder from Jurgen Klopp on international duty

View 3 Images Florian Wirtz failed to impress again (Image: Robin Jones - AFC Bournemouth/AFC Bournemouth via Getty Images)

Football fans should know by now. It's hard to argue with Jamie Carragher.

‌



The Liverpool legend is one of the most respected pundits in the game, firm but fair. And no more was that the case than in his analysis of Florian Wirtz after Liverpool ground out a 1-0 win at Bournemouth.

‌



"That was one of the poorest I've ever seen him in a Liverpool shirt." Carragher declared on his Sky Sports podcast. Against a Bournemouth side who'd played away in Europe on the Thursday night, and with Alexander Isak, Bradley Barcola, Cody Gakpo and Dominik Szoboszlai set to spread Cherries' defence thin, it was supposed be an afternoon on which Wirtz stamped his authority.

‌



But Sunday went differently, as Wirtz ultimately came off in the 73rd minute with the jury still out for many. Not for Carragher, though.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



"I don't think Wirtz is in poor form since he came to Liverpool," the ex-centre-back added. "I actually think what we're seeing is what he is.

That's a far cry from Jurgen Klopp's verdict. "Exceptional", "once in a century" - that's just some of the praise which the Germany manager has showered onto Wirtz since his £116million move to Anfield in 2025.

Now, after all the talk, Klopp gets to work with him. The playmaker is one of 44 players who've received call-ups from the former Liverpool manager ahead of the two-week international window.

‌



Should Andoni Iraola drop Florian Wirtz? Have your say in the comments section.

View 3 Images Jurgen Klopp is a big fan of Florian Wirtz (Image: Alex Grimm/Getty Images)

As Klopp splits his squad in two, Wirtz will only feature in Germany's final two games against Serbia and Greece, notably missing their Nations League opener against the Netherlands. With due respect to Serbia and Greece, those are two opponents which the 23-year-old should be relishing facing.

‌



Klopp is braced for inquests into Wirtz's performances, but says that that expectations need to be lowered. "We need to be satisfied when Flo Wirtz plays a game in which he gave everything but didn't register a goal or assist," the German stressed.

"We simply need to give the boy the feeling, 'That was more than good enough today. You helped us as a team. We won 1-0 or 2-0'."

View 3 Images Jamie Carragher would drop Florian Wirtz from Liverpool's line-up (Image: James Gill - Danehouse/Getty Images)

‌



Andoni Iraola seems to be listening, saying in a post-match interview: "I think we improved [during the game against Bournemouth]. Florian has helped us also to improve. Second half he was playing much better, he was finding better spots to receive and turn."

But Wirtz's managers can't defend him forever. He needs to deliver - or else Iraola's patience could run out.

As Carragher warned: "The last hope is that Jurgen Klopp can do something special and he comes back [better]. But if you're asking me, with Liverpool going back into a run of games against top opposition - Manchester City at home - he can't be in the team."

Sports.title: Ex-Man Utd star in talks over Russia move after rejecting crazy offer from Libya
Sports.content:
Ex-Man Utd star in talks over Russia move after rejecting crazy offer from Libya

Manchester United paid £36 million for a player who is now fielding wild contract offers from Libya and Russia as a free agent after being offered around Europe

View 2 Images Anthony Martial left Monterrey almost four months ago and is still without a club (Image: Jam Media, Getty Images)

Russian Premier League clubs are reportedly in contact with Anthony Martial over signing the former Manchester United forward. Libyan Premier League side Al-Ittihad Tripoli are said to have already seen a contract offer worth £13million rejected by the free agent.

‌



Martial, 30, left Liga MX team Monterrey midway through a two-year contract earlier this summer. He is apparently now wanted by multiple clubs in Spain, including Malaga.

‌



The former France international left United two years ago and eventually joining Super League Greece side AEK Athens. He is now looking for his third club after spending nine seasons at Old Trafford.

‌



L'Equipe claims CSKA Moscow and Krasnodar are amongst several clubs keen on Martial. The forward is believed to have rejected an approach from Auxerre earlier in the summer.

They are understood to be the sole French club to have tabled an offer for him despite agents allegedly touting his availability to numerous others. Lens and Nice have previously been linked with a move.

Everton were even mentioned at one point after the summer transfer window closed without another forward arriving on Merseyside following their deadline-day debacle with Folarin Balogun. Several other Premier League clubs were said to be offered him.

‌



View 2 Images Anthony Martial spent nine seasons at Manchester United before leaving as a free agent two years ago (Image: Alex Livesey, Getty Images)

Foot Mercato claims Martial knocked back Al-Ittihad Tripoli's offer worth a net salary of £8.6million across two years, alongside a £4.3million signing-on fee. Libya's most successful club brought in former Southampton winger and the Morocco international Sofiane Boufal earlier this month.

Lorient sporting director Laurent Koscielny has revealed they were approached about signing Martial. The former Arsenal defender told Ouest-France: "I think we received 400 to 450 player offers during the transfer window.

‌



"There were, for example, a lot of former internationals in the lot, including Anthony Martial." The duo represented France together on 13 occasions during their international careers.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Martial has featured in only 53 matches across the two campaigns since his Old Trafford exit. The striker netted nine times for AEK but registered just a single goal for Monterrey before heading back to Europe.

Article continues below

He will celebrate his 31st birthday in early December and was said to be holding off on any decision regarding his future until this international break. Martial has previous experience of Spanish football from his loan spell at Sevilla, with Malaga located just under 100 miles southeast of Andalucia's capital.

A switch to Russia, however, would represent a leap into the unknown. Clubs in the nation are also barred from UEFA competitions following the invasion of Ukraine.

Sports.title: Gary Lineker tears into Man Utd co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe - 'Unpleasant human being'
Sports.content:
Gary Lineker tears into Man Utd co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe - 'Unpleasant human being'

Sir Jim Ratcliffe was back in the headlines last week after criticising the UK Government's approach to immigration - before Manchester United slipped to another poor result

View 3 Images Gary Lineker gave a stinging assessment (Image: The Rest is Football)

Gary Lineker has branded Sir Jim Ratcliffe an 'unpleasant human being' - and that claimed the Manchester United co-owner is 'even worse than the Glazers'.

‌



It's the latest criticism to be levelled at Ratcliffe following a difficult weekend both inside and outside of football. On Saturday, the billionaire said that 'nobody's tough enough to deal with the immigration problem' in the UK, having claimed earlier this year that the nation had been 'colonised by immigrants'.

‌



His comments prompted the Manchester United Muslim Supporters Club to call for Ratcliffe's exit, saying that the INEOS chairman 'must go'. Things didn't improve on Sunday, as United produced a woeful performance before rescuing a 1-1 draw at Fulham, who went into the match bottom of the Premier League table.

‌



Now Lineker has waded in with a stinging assessment of Ratcliffe and the club which he owns 28.94 per cent of after joining forces with the Glazer family in February 2024. "I look at Man United and I see problems coming down from the top," the England legend said on The Rest is Football podcast.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



"I must congratulate the Glazers on finding someone even worse than them that they can blame and getting him in there and getting all the stick: Jim Ratcliffe.

"He's clearly... I don't think he's a particularly pleasant human being and it's a bit of shambles of a football club the way it's being run at the moment. So, well done to the Glazers on that one, deflecting everything away from them!"

Lineker also made reference to another pressing issue for United, with 15-year-old wonderkid JJ Gabriel demanding to leave due to a lack of first-team opportunities. "It is a bit of a mess that club," the ex-striker continued.

‌



"You've got a ground that's falling apart, all sorts of complaints about various things. They're losing young teenagers, it looks like that [Gabriel leaving] is going to happen.

"The results, the inconsistency seems to be back. They have backed the manager lots of times and it's not worked for them but there's got to be something dripping down from the top."

Are Manchester United better off under Sir Jim Ratclife? Have your say in the comments section.

‌



View 3 Images Manchester United have started the season in dire form (Image: Tiego Grenho/MI News/NurPhoto via Getty Images)

It remains to be seen if Ratcliffe will row back on his comments, like when he offered a mealy-mouthed apology for his colonisation claim. Then Prime Minister Sir Keir Starmer had urged the 73-year-old to apologise, calling Ratcliffe's words 'offensive and wrong'.

Lineker didn't make much of the apology, saying: "The hypocrisy I find difficult. Obviously, Keir Starmer has called for him to make an apology; whether he will or not remains to be seen.

‌



"I watched it and the hypocrisy really - the guy's a migrant himself, an economic migrant [because] he lives in Monaco. You can have a gripe all you like, but at least be here, pay taxes, and contribute to our society.

"I would say a lot of these migrants who come in contribute enormously and facts show you that in terms of revenue and paid tax. Whereas Jim out there, in Monaco, is doing everything he can to avoid paying tax, I would suggest.

View 3 Images Sir Jim Ratcliffe has faced calls to leave Manchester United (Image: Bo Amstrup/Ritzau Scanpix/AFP via Getty Images))

‌



"Also, you're one of the owners of Manchester United, a club that has a lot of players from overseas. When he's talking about colonised with immigrants, is it okay that you're a white person living abroad, not a brown or black person? I don't know, only he can answer that question.

"Lots and lots of my friends who support United have come on and said similar things to what I'm saying now, they're very disappointed. Look at the story of [how] Amad has ended up here. So I find it deeply concerning that an owner of a football club can say that sort of thing."

Over the weekend, the petrochemicals mogul spoke in Denmark at the launch of the EU's first carbon capture and storage system. It was there where Ratcliffe stated that he'd lost confidence in the UK, adding: "We had the greatest empire in the world. We were a great people. We won two world wars."

Article continues below

He went on to say: "Nobody's tough enough to deal with the immigration problem. Nobody's tough enough to deal with the benefits problem. But somebody needs to do it."

Sports.title: Michael Owen singles out Man Utd star as 'weak link' after summer transfer blow
Sports.content:
Michael Owen singles out Man Utd star as 'weak link' after summer transfer blow

Manchester United's struggles continued on Sunday and Marcus Rashford has been singled out for particular criticism as the team's attack fails to fire

View 2 Images Michael Owen has singled out one of Manchester United's attackers (Image: Getty)

Michael Owen has described Marcus Rashford as 'the weak link' in Manchester United's struggling forward line.

‌



Rashford is back in the fold at Old Trafford following successive loan spells away, which saw him go more than 18 months without playing for his boyhood club. He was handed the No.9 shirt this term and been regularly called upon by Michael Carrick.

‌



However, the England international, amid the odd moment of quality, is yet to register a single goal or assist in over 400 minutes of football in all competitions. United have scored eight times in five games, but five of those goals came in one game.

‌



Rashford, alongside the likes of Bryan Mbeumo, Matheus Cunha and Benjamin Sesko, is struggling to consistently impact games - but Owen has singled out Rashford as the biggest under performer.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



The ex-Liverpool striker said on Premier League Productions: "On the left, Marcus Rashford has been probably the quietest of those attackers. He was quiet again today in his body language, just the glum face. He just doesn’t seem to be loving his football which has been a permanent frustration with Marcus.

"It does look like the weight of the world is on his shoulders and you just think how? Why? He’s living everybody’s dream. Surely there’s something behind the scenes that is making him look as if he’s not enjoying his football at the moment."

Rashford came back to Manchester off the back of his season in Spain with Barcelona and with Ruben Amorim, whom he clashed with, no longer at the helm, which presented a way back.

‌



View 2 Images Marcus Rashford is yet to score this season

Owen concedes that the Catalans' decision to not activate the purchase option in Rashford's loan agreement and instead spend nearly three times as much to sign compatriot Anthony Gordon was a telling sign that there clearly were doubts.

"Last chance saloon was Barcelona," he said. "I couldn’t believe his luck in getting a team like Barcelona. He does reasonably well out there, but not well enough for them to keep him and then they end up spending fortunes to replace him by buying Anthony Gordon.

Article continues below

"So, it wasn’t all perfect. It wasn’t all rosy despite any spin that people put on it. And then he comes back to Manchester United. He’s done okay, but only okay.

"There’s a bit of a demand for Benjamin Sesko to come back in and start, injury permitting of course. But if that happens, Cunha is going to go on the left and Rashford would be the weak link in that attack as things stand."

Sports.title: PSG chief Nasser Al-Khelaifi 'under investigation' over broadcasting conflict
Sports.content:
PSG chief Nasser Al-Khelaifi 'under investigation' over broadcasting conflict

Paris Saint-Germain president, Nasser Al-Khelaifi is the subject of an ongoing investigation in France as a result of suspicion of a conflict of interests regarding broadcasting rights

View Image Nasser Al-Khelaifi is being investigated in France (Image: Anadolu via Getty Images)

Nasser Al-Khelaifi is reportedly under investigation in France due to a suspected illegal conflict of interest with regards to broadcasting rights. The Qatari mogul is the president of Paris Saint-Germain, but also holds stewardship with the beIN Media Group.

‌



A preliminary probe is linked with both positions, and involves a meeting regarding broadcasting rights with the French football league's representatives from July 2024. The meeting came a day after beIN made a €100million offer for the rights to broadcast one Ligue 1 match per week.

‌



The league later accepted the offer. The most recent investigation into Al-Khelaifi was launched back in April off the back of a tip from Anticor. Proceedings have also been passed on to anti-corruption and finance police.

‌



Arsenal sent JJ Gabriel transfer warning after Man Utd exit demand READ MORE :

Victor Munoz speaks out about Liverpool team-mates as he admits being shocked after move READ MORE :

As per RFI, a source close to the case says that Anticor claim Al-Khelaifi took part in discussions regarding the validation of the bid from beIN Sports. That's despite serving as the chairman of beIN Media Group, which is claimed to have created a conflict of interest.

The source also alleges that Al-Khelaifi put pressure on other Ligue 1 club presidents to support the proposal from beIN Sports. However, Renaud Semerdjian - who serves as Al-Khelaifi's lawyer - has rejected such claims.

He told AFP: "The allegations made against Mr Nasser Al-Khelaifi are without basis, neither legally nor factually," while adding that the PSG president had "always acted in an independent, impartial and objective manner."

‌



Al-Khelaifi has held his position with PSG since a 2011 takeover of the club spearheaded by Qatar Sports Investments. However, he has seen a number of legal challenges in the years since.

Last February, the 52-year-old was charged with complicity in abuse of power concerning shareholder voting with a company. Meanwhile, Al-Khelaifi has also seen previous charges for alleged corruption over Qatari bids for the 2017 and 2019 World Athletics Championships.

These were ultimately annulled by France's Court of Cassation in February 2023, given the country's judicial system did not have a right to prosecute.

It comes as Al-Khelaifi ruled out any chance of him running to succeed Gianni Infantino as FIFA president when next year's election lands.

‌



The 56-year-old has seen calls for his job following a controversial World Cup in North America, on top of failed proposals to sell stakes in the tournament to private investors under a scheme he revealed as the FIFA Forward Enterprise.

However, Al-Khelaifi said in August that he has no intentions of tossing his name in the hat for Infantino's position with World Football when the elections land in March.

He explained at the time: "I am very happy being president of Paris Saint-Germain, and happy to continue in this position."

‌

‌

Sports.title: Jose Mourinho's wildest moments as Real Madrid boss goes full Jose in latest outburst
Sports.content:
Jose Mourinho's wildest moments as Real Madrid boss goes full Jose in latest outburst

Real Madrid boss Jose Mourinho has added to the list of memorable moments from his managerial career

View 5 Images Jose Mourinho has had an eventful managerial career (Image: Diego Souto/Getty Images)

Real Madrid boss Jose Mourinho has added to his catalogue of controversial moments following his side’s defeat to Atletico Madrid. The Portuguese coach has fuelled rivalries, slammed refereeing decisions and clashed with opposition managers throughout his decades in the dugout.

‌



Mourinho could not prevent Los Blancos from losing the Madrid derby as goals from Jonathan David and Alejandro Grimaldo saw off his 10-man side. However, the 63-year-old, who is famed for his press conference outbursts, produced pictures of two tackles from Atletico’s Cristian Romero and Lee Kang-in, which avoided red cards, while also focusing on the appointment of referee Miguel Angel Ortiz Arias

‌



“It’s all been very strange. The referee was known a week in advance… and he isn’t an international referee, which suggests he isn’t exactly a top-tier official,” the Real boss said. “The poor guy came here and couldn’t handle the pressure.”

‌



It is the latest high-profile incident from Mourinho, who first made waves in English football with his touchline celebration against Manchester United as Porto boss and later dubbed himself “a special one” when being unveiled as Chelsea manager in 2004. Here is a look at some of the wildest moments from his coaching career.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‘Enemy of football’

The then-Chelsea boss was branded “an enemy of football” by UEFA referees' committee chairman Volker Roth in 2005. The issue stemmed from Mourinho’s accusations that referee Anders Frisk and Barcelona coach Frank Rijkaard had spoken during half-time of a Champions League match, with Didier Drogba later being sent off for the Blues after the interval.

‌



Rijkaard insisted that Frsk had sent him away, while the referee came under intense scrutiny and received death threats in the aftermath before choosing to retire in March 2005. Reacting to Frisk’s decision, refereeing chief Roth said: “We can't accept that one of our best referees has been forced to quit because of this. People like Mourinho are the enemy of football.”

Hiding in laundry basket

Mourinho received a two-game ban from UEFA, which prevented the manager from being on the sideline for his team’s quarter-final clash with Bayern Munich. However, the master tactician snuck into the dressing room after getting to Stamford Bridge several hours before the game.

“I went there and nobody saw me. The problem was to leave after,” he later admitted to beIN Sport. “And Stewart Bannister the kit man put me in the basket. It was a little bit open so I could breathe.

‌



“But when he is taking it outside the dressing room, the UEFA guys were following and desperate to find me so he closed the box and I couldn't breathe! When he opened the box I was dying! I am serious! I was claustrophobic, I promise! It's true!”

View 5 Images Mourinho had a notable rivalry with long-serving Arsenal manager Arsene Wenger (Image: Shaun Botterill/Getty Images)

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



Arsene Wenger feud

Upon arriving for his first stint as Chelsea boss, Arsenal were reigning Premier League champions and Mourinho developed a rivalry with Gunners boss Arsene Wenger. In 2005, he referred to Wenger as “a voyeur” over a perceived obsession with Chelsea, prompting the Arsenal manager to consider legal action.

Mourinho later apologised for having overstepped the mark with his comment. However, he later branded Wenger a “specialist in failure” during his second stint in charge of Chelsea.

“If he is right and I am afraid of failure it is because I didn't fail many times. Eight years without silverware, that's failure,” Mourinho said in 2014 before referencing Arsenal’s trophy drought. “He's a specialist in failure. If I do that in Chelsea, eight years, I leave and don't come back.”

‌



Eye poke incident

During his first spell at Real Madrid, Mourinho became involved in a scuffle with Barcelona’s coaching staff. The two rivals met in the Spanish Super Cup in 2011 and a tackle from Marcelo on Barcelona’s Cesc Fabregas led to a confrontation between the two benches.

Mourinho was seen poking the eye of Barcelona assistant coach Tito Vilanova. He received a two-match ban for his actions. The Real Madrid manager said of the incident: “I was the one in the wrong, I shouldn't have done what I did. Of course not, that negative image stays forever. Tito had nothing to do with it. I apologise to him.”

View 5 Images Jose Mourinho gouges Tito Vilanova's eye at the end of the second leg of the Spanish Super Cup between Real Madrid and Barcelona in 2011 (Image: Sky Sports)

‌



Car park rant

In 2023, Roma boss Mourinho made his feelings clear after losing the Europa League final to Sevilla. English referee Anthony Taylor had been in charge of the match and Mourinho vented his frustrations in the car park, saying: “You were a f****** disgrace tonight. It is a disgrace.” However, the manager denied that his comments were directed at Taylor, aiming his ire at UEFA refereeing chief Roberto Rosetti.

“Taylor wasn’t there. Taylor was still in the ground,” Mourinho said. “Other people, not Taylor. The fourth official, his assistants, Rosetti, Howard Webb, the technical director of the PGMOL.

“Everything ends, we go back into the dressing room, I go down to the garage and the refereeing team come in. I’ve got a good relationship with Webb and Rosetti. They’ve both refereed my games. I know it wasn’t elegant, but I didn’t insult anyone.

‌



“I went over to Rosetti and said: ‘Ref’ — that’s what I call him — ‘ref, is it a penalty or isn’t it a penalty?’ Rosetti did what refs usually do. He didn’t reply. I asked Webb the same question. He put his hand on my shoulder and said: ‘Yes, Jose, it’s a pen’.”

View 5 Images Jose Mourinho was unhappy with referee Anthony Taylor during the 2023 Europa League final (Image: Giuseppe Maffia/NurPhoto via Getty Images)

Respect, respect, respect

Mourinho made several memorable comments during his time as Manchester United boss. In March 2018, he had blamed “football heritage” for the club’s shortcomings in the post-Ferguson era. He would later describe finishing second in the Premier League with United as one of his best-ever achievements.

‌



Following a 3-0 defeat to Spurs in August 2018, Mourinho repeated “respect, respect, respect,” as he stormed out of his post-match press conference. He was sacked by the club that December.

After the 3-0 loss, Mourinho said: “Do you know what the result was? Three-nil. Do you know what this means (holding up three fingers)?

"Three-nil, but it also means three Premier Leagues and I won more alone than the other 19 managers together. Three for me and two for them.”

‌



Altercation with Galatasaray boss

Mourinho’s time in Turkey as Fenerbahce manager was marked by several controversial moments. In April 2025, after losing to Galatasaray in the Turkish Cup, he clashed with his opposite number, Okan Buruk.

While both managers were speaking with the officiating team after the game, Mourinho appeared to pinch Buruk’s nose, with the Galatasaray boss falling to the floor in response. He was subsequently given a three-match ban.

View 5 Images Galatasaray manager Okan Buruk fell to the floor after an altercation with Mourinho (Image: Murat Akbas/ dia images via Getty Images)

‌



Protesting decision with laptop

Earlier in his Fenerbahce tenure, Mourinho found a unique way to challenge a referee’s decision. Mourinho felt that a goal against Antalyaspor had been incorrectly ruled out for offside and sought to take action by placing a laptop in front of a broadcast camera.

The screen showed a freeze-frame of the decision he felt had unfairly gone against his side in September 2024. He was booked for his antics during the game.

Wearing a wire

As Roma boss, Mourinho made headlines after admitting he had worn a wire to record his interactions during a 1-1 draw with Monza in May 2023. He described referee Daniele Chiffi as "the worst I've ever encountered” and took extra steps regarding his communication with the officials.

Article continues below

“I'm not stupid, you know - today, I went to the game with a microphone,” he said. “I recorded everything. From the moment I left the locker room to the moment I returned. I protected myself.”

Sports.title: Rock-bottom Tottenham facing familiar question after huge error under Roberto De Zerbi
Sports.content:
Rock-bottom Tottenham facing familiar question after huge error under Roberto De Zerbi

Tottenham Hotspur spent heavily in the summer to avoid another battle against relegation under Roberto De Zerbi but things appear to have gotten even worse for the North London side

View 4 Images Tottenham boss Roberto De Zerbi feels the heat (Image: Getty Images)

The huge summer spending spree was supposed to ensure it did not happen again. Even the most pessimistic Tottenham fan would struggle to believe things would not improve this season - and yet the Premier League table makes for grim reading.

‌



Surely no-one thought at the start of the season that Tottenham would be in this state after five games. One bookie has them 13/2 to go down.

‌



And it begs the familiar question: are Tottenham too good to go down?

‌



Tottenham have hit a new low because they have hit rock bottom. They are winless, are bottom of the table for the duration of the three week international window. It’s unthinkable. First game back on October 10? Manchester United away. Thanks for that.

After two consecutive 17th place finishes, Roberto De Zerbi was supposed to oversee a major lift in the club’s fortunes.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Never again. That was the message after last season’s near miss saw them flirt with relegation which, in reality, was never really a possibility the previous year. They finished 13 points above the drop zone in 2024/25.

Last season, it was genuinely too close for comfort. Two points ahead of West Ham and safety was only secured on the final day.

‌



They spent around £380m on huge signings in the summer, proven Premier League players and the vision was that De Zerbi would oversee a dramatic change in fortunes.

Sandro Tonali was the biggest buy, Matheus Fernandes was not far behind but they also brought in Omar Marmoush, Savio, Jan Paul van Hecke, Andy Robertson, Tosin Adarabioyo and Marcos Senesi.

There is a lot of quality there. A complete squad overhaul. And maybe that is part of the problem because it is hard to gel so many new players for them to click straight away.

‌



View 4 Images Spurs look set to endure another miserable season (Image: Getty Images)

They deliberately recruited big characters like Robertson and Tosin to address the distinct lack of leadership. Again, smart business.

Tottenham undoubtedly overpaid on some players but, after those back-to-back 17th place finishes, they were always going to have to in terms of contracts and also probably fees.

‌



That is how you persuade selling clubs and players to join a club which is not in Europe and spent the last two years floundering in the lower reaches of the table.

The one thing they did not do was buy an out-and-out forward and went into the season relying on Dominic Solanke. And that has to be an error. Perhaps the biggest of all. Solanke looks so short of confidence.

They have some versatile forwards in there but even Marmoush is not exactly a classic No9. They are creating chances - but are just not putting them away.

‌



View 4 Images Tottenham splashed the cash this summer (Image: Getty Images)

Against Aston Villa on Saturday, they should have been 3-0 up at half time. But the lack of confidence, the nerves in the stadium among the fans and the doubts among the players made life so difficult.

You have to question the logic of going to Australia and New Zealand in pre-season and once a club does that you cannot expect too much sympathy when it comes to players being fatigued and tired - especially after a World Cup year.

‌



The fans have backed the team and, even against Villa, they were loud and supportive as Tottenham started well… and then faded away and crumbled again.

They were beset by basic defensive errors. The defending on Nicolas Jackson’s goal was so bad that no wonder it left De Zerbi tearing his hair out.

But while De Zerbi brings passion, attacking ideals and determination to the table, he also brings a history of losing the plot and meltdowns. Nine clubs in 13 years.

‌



View 4 Images Spurs have yet to win this season (Image: Getty Images)

Let’s make no mistake about it, if this was a more established manager, they would be facing questions about his future. Tottenham cannot be bottom after five games. At least they scored against Villa.

But De Zerbi was brought in to save an ailing club last season, that was mission accomplished and then they backed him in the market. You have to - and they will - stick with him.

Article continues below

It has, however, exposed a club with more problems than we first thought. There is simply no way Spurs will go down this season. No chance. They have got way too much quality. In answer to the question: too good to go down? Absolutely.

But any idea that they could push for Europe - I had them in the top half and looking upwards - now seems wildly optimistic and naive. But this is a going to be a long and somewhat painful road back to where the club feels it belongs.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"
