World.title: Court junks rejection of petition to probe Sonia voter roll entry
World.content:
NEW DELHI: A Delhi court has set aside a 2025 magisterial order rejecting a plea to probe alleged irregularities in the inclusion of Sonia Gandhi's name in the electoral rolls. It observed that the "impugned order suffers from manifest errors in law".

Special judge Vishal Gogne of Dwarka courts remanded the matter to the ACJM for a fresh, reasoned order after an inquiry and after hearing the concerned police officer. It will be listed on Sept 29. He said the order was "non-speaking" and lacked reasons. There was no discussion on the sequence of Sonia's inclusion, deletion and re-inclusion in the electoral rolls of 1980, 1982 and 1983, he said. Advocate Vikas Tripathi's complaint alleged that Sonia's name was unlawfully entered in the electoral roll for New Delhi parliamentary constituency in 1980, before she acquired Indian citizenship.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Her name was allegedly deleted in 1982 and re-entered in 1983, with the complaint claiming the re-entry, too, preceded her acquisition of citizenship on April 30, 1983.

In 2025, ACJM dismissed the complaint as "based on bald assertions unaccompanied by essential particulars of cheating and forgery" and described the material as the "photocopy of the photocopy of the uncertified electoral roll of 1980". Tripathi challenged the order before sessions court in Dec 2025. On Monday, Gogne said such an allegation of "tampering with the electoral rules, fraudulent inclusion of the name of a voter, inclusion of the name of a non-citizen and possible use of false declaration" merits a "reasoned order" on whether cheating and forgery were disclosed.

World.title: No median cuts, surface intersections on future high-speed NH corridors: NHAI
World.content:
A view of the Barapullah Phase-3 elevated corridor that is scheduled to be inaugurated on September 29, 2026, in New Delhi on Saturday. (ANI Photo)

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: New access-controlled high-speed national highway corridors will have no median (divider) openings and no at-grade (surface level) intersections, a move that aims at eliminating conflict points and reducing crashes.It has also been mandated under new NHAI guidelines issued on Monday that these corridors wonât have raised concrete dividers but flush medians â painted centre lanes with thick wire ropes or crash barriers. These will also have advance exit signage at 5 km, 2 km, 1 km and 500 metres to help motorists prepare for lane changes well in advance.The design provisions are aimed at improving safety on access-controlled corridors where cars are allowed to travel at speeds of up to 100 kmph. Delhi-Dehradun Expressway, Ambala-Kotputli corridor and Trans-Haryana corridor are among such highways.NHAI said the guidelines seek to bring uniformity in the planning and design of access-controlled high-speed corridors and ensure consistency in technical standards across projects.âThe guidelines will apply to all upcoming four-lane and six-lane greenfield and brownfield access-controlled high-speed national highways,â an NHAI spokesperson said.Officials said eliminating median cuts and surface intersections will prevent dangerous cross movements and wrong-side driving, while standardised signage and geometric design will improve traffic flow and reduce the risk of high-speed crashes on the new generation of national highway corridors.The move is significant as govt has set a target of developing 50,000 km of access-controlled high-speed corridors over the coming years.At present, there are no separate standards governing the planning and design of access-controlled high-speed national highways, except for expressways. The new document fills that gap by laying down dedicated norms for highways that are access-controlled but not classified as expressways.The guidelines also specify lane configuration based on detailed traffic assessment and future traffic projections. Depending on the expected traffic volume and the number of structures such as bridges, flyovers and interchanges, these corridors will have a right of way of 60 metres or 70 metres.

World.title: Paneer, khoya, sweets in focus as Delhi steps up food adulteration checks ahead of festive season
World.content:
As sacks of khoya and paneer arrive in Delhi’s markets and sweet shops stock up for the festive rush, the Delhi Police Crime Branch is stepping up intelligence-gathering on food adulteration.

The watch comes amid a series of food safety seizures and inspections across Delhi. More than 2,800 kg of unsafe and abandoned khoya and butter were found in major markets earlier this month. Ten khoya and cream samples collected from Mori Gate were found to be non-conforming, while four paneer samples from Janakpuri Mandi tested positive for detergent. Around 150 kg of paneer and 10 kg of khoya were subsequently destroyed.

The Food Safety Department also seized 508 kg of spurious paneer at Okhla Sabzi Mandi and destroyed over 131 kg of expired food items, including gram flour, khoya and wheat flour, during inspections of sweet manufacturing units and mandis.

“With the festive season approaching, the Crime Branch has been on alert to identify leads related to food adulteration. As soon as we receive information about food adulteration, it is shared with the Delhi government’s Food Safety Department. The information and timing of the operation are coordinated with the department, following which joint raids are conducted,” said Special Commissioner of Police (Crime) H.G.S. Dhaliwal.

The police, however, do not independently test suspected food products. Deputy Commissioner of Police (Crime) Aditya Gautam said food safety officers accompanying the police during raids collect samples for laboratory testing.

Common adulterants

Mr. Gautam said investigators had found rangkat or hydro powder (sodium hydrosulfite), being used to give khoya and sweets a whiter appearance, sawdust mixed with cumin, brick powder with chilli powder, and chemicals and hydrogenated vegetable oil used to adulterate ghee.

Speaking to The Hindu, Devesh Mahla, Director, Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) - North India, said the nature of milk adulteration has also changed.

“Earlier, they used to mix water in milk, which was not necessarily dangerous, but now, as the demand and greed have increased, they have started preparing synthetic milk made of chemicals, including detergents, shampoo, caustic soda and urea,” he said.

Mr. Gautam said accused persons often change locations after an operation, making subsequent raids at the same premises uncommon.

Food safety checks

Mr. Mahla said, raids were based on consumer complaints and risk-based assessment of food items. Milk, meat, ghee, khoya and eggs are among the categories assessed as higher risk, he said.

Food safety officers are authorised under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, to inspect premises, verify FSSAI licences and documents and collect samples for laboratory testing. “The report is used to prosecute the offender,” Mr. Mahla said.

Mr. Mahla said registered food businesses could be subjected to regular surveillance, surprise inspections and sampling, while unregistered establishments, including roadside food vendors and outlets in food streets, often remained outside routine surveillance until a complaint is received.

Depending on the nature of the offence, police can invoke Sections 274 and 275 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita for food adulteration and the sale of noxious or unfit food, and Section 318 in cases of cheating. Provisions relating to tampering with or counterfeiting property marks can be invoked when fake packaging or brands are used. Sections 105 and 110, dealing with culpable homicide not amounting to murder and attempt to commit culpable homicide, respectively, may apply if adulteration causes death or serious injury.

Mr. Mahla urged consumers to check whether food businesses have the appropriate FSSAI registration or licence and to be aware of what they are consuming. Suspected adulteration can be reported through FSSAI’s Food Safety Connect platform or its official website.

World.title: 'Historic occasion': Jaishankar describes first V4+India Foreign Ministers meeting
World.content:
India and the four-member Visegrad group of Central European countries on Monday (September 21, 2026) agreed to step up political, economic and defence cooperation at their first Foreign Ministers' meeting, which External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar described as a “new historic occasion”.

The Visegrad Group (V4) is a cultural and political alliance of the Czech Republic, Hungary, Poland, and Slovakia that aims to advance cooperation in military, economic, cultural, and energy affairs.

The first meeting between the Foreign Ministers of the Visegrad Group and India was held on Monday (September 21, 2026), on the sidelines of the 81st session of the UN General Assembly.

Mr Jaishankar met with Poland's Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs, Radek Sikorski; Hungary's Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister, Anita Orban; Slovakia's Minister of Foreign and European Affairs, Juraj Blanar; and the Czech Minister of Foreign Affairs, Petr Macinka.

"It was, in a sense, a new historic occasion,” Mr. Jaishankar said in remarks after the meeting.

"It was a very, very productive meeting. What we agreed was that since India's relationship with the European Union itself is deepening, with the V4 we would take some special initiatives to create an annual business forum,” he said, adding that there was “consensus" that the Foreign Ministers of the five nations in the group would meet annually.

“We would also explore technology and innovation whether we could be doing more. We have a very strong history with all the V4 countries in defence. We want to refresh and take forward that record and that cooperation,” Mr. Jaishankar said.

The group also discussed issues including space, connectivity, and people-to-people mobility.

Mr. Jaishankar said the meeting was “very worthwhile” and “very productive”, with discussions focusing on cooperation as well as major global crises, including the Ukraine conflict and developments in the Gulf.

“It was really a very, very worthwhile, very productive meeting. I'm very pleased about it,” he said in remarks to reporters after the meeting.

In a post on X, Mr. Jaishankar said the first meeting in the V4+India format agreed to closer political cooperation, including annual meetings of foreign ministers, and deeper economic cooperation, including the Annual Business Forum.

Delighted to join the Visegrád Group DPM & FM @radeksikorski#Poland DPM & FM @_OrbanAnita#Hungary FM Juraj Blanár #Slovakia and FM @petr_macinka#Czechia on the sidelines of #UNGA81. Our first meeting in the V4+India format agreed to:



✅ Closer political cooperation including… pic.twitter.com/mBqMTkC6QN — Dr. S. Jaishankar (@DrSJaishankar) September 21, 2026

The countries also agreed to strengthen technology, innovation, research and education partnerships; reinvigorate defence cooperation; further develop cultural cooperation and people-to-people relations and work together to support multilateralism, he said.

Mr. Jaishankar also said that India has “very good” relations with the V4 countries.

"These are countries with a very strong, very distinctive capability. These are industrial economies, economies with great innovation and technology talent, and I think how the V4 come together is for them to decide. But we certainly welcome the opportunity to work with the V4 together,” he told reporters.

World.title: CNN, MS NOW, Politico to sue Trump administration over White House access
World.content:
CNN, MS NOW, and Politico will sue the Trump administration after being denied access to the White House, the news outlets said in a joint statement on Monday (September 21, 2026).

President Donald Trump said Friday (September 18) he was banning the outlets from the presidential mansion as punishment for distributing what he calls "fake news."

"This morning, we notified the government that we are filing a lawsuit today to protect our First Amendment rights and defend the principle that the government does not decide what the press reports or publishes," the statement said.

Also Read: U.S. television networks halt Trump coverage in revolt over White House ban

The outlets said the White House revoked their journalists’ credentials “without notice or process” because it “objected to our reporting.”

“Left unchallenged, this threatens press freedom and the public’s right to independent journalism free from government interference,” they said.

Mr. Trump did not detail what prompted the ban but said, “Media outlets shouldn’t be able to constantly write or report FICTION and LIES when they’re covering the President of the United States.”

The 80-year-old Republican — who has long had a fiery relationship with the mainstream media — warned Friday (September 18) that other outlets could face a similar fate but did not say which ones.

CNN had been scheduled to serve Monday (September 21) as the White House TV pool, a rotating assignment in which a broadcaster films on behalf of all television outlets for the day. Updated guidance from the White House late Sunday (September 20) simply listed a back-up crew.

World.title: Rain slows movement on several Bengaluru roads
World.content:
Light to moderate rains, which continued intermittently across parts of Bengaluru on Monday, slowed traffic on several roads during the evening peak hours, with waterlogging adding to the congestion in some areas.

Traffic was slow on stretches around Bagalur Cross, B. Narayanapura, Marathahalli-Kadubeesanahalli, and Manyata-Veerannapalya. At Bagalur Cross, waterlogging affected traffic movement towards both the city and the airport, while the Marathahalli-Kadubeesanahalli and Manyata-Veerannapalya stretches witnessed heavy congestion during peak hours, the Bengaluru traffic police said.

Traffic police and Greater Bengaluru Authority (GBA) officials said teams attended to complaints of waterlogging and took measures to clear the accumulated water and prevent prolonged stagnation.

GBA officials also carried out cleaning works at several waterlogging-prone locations, clearing garbage, plastic waste, and other debris that was obstructing the flow of rainwater into drains.

In the Shantinagar division, cleaning was carried out along M.G. Road and Chinnaswamy Stadium Road, while similar work was taken up at vulnerable locations in Gandhinagar, the GBA said. The rain also led to tree and branch falls at several locations across the city between 6 p.m. and 8.30 p.m.

World.title: Morning Digest: 17.66 lakh names struck off from Odisha’s final electoral roll; Trump praises Mamdani after New York meeting, and more
World.content:
Odisha’s final electoral roll has 3.16 crore voters; 17.66 lakh names struck off

Odisha’s final electoral roll published on Monday (September 21, 2026) has 3,16,32,754 voters, a decrease of 17,66,837 from the pre-Special Intensive Revision (SIR) figure, according to the Office of the Chief Electoral Officer (CEO).

Trump praises leftist Mamdani after meeting in New York

U.S. President Donald Trump heaped praise Monday (September 21, 2026) on New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani as the pair set aside their political differences to discuss immigration enforcement and a multi-billion dollar housing project.

Trump, in call with Yemen President, did not pledge military support against Houthis, say sources

U.S. President Donald ‌Trump spoke by phone with ​Yemeni President Rashad ⁠al-Alimi on Sunday (September 20, 2026), four people familiar with the matter said, discussing the ‌advances of the Iran-backed Houthis around a vital ‌global waterway.

Paramount reaches deal with states to settle their case challenging Warner buyout, AP source say

Skydance-owned Paramount reached a settlement on Monday (September 21, 2026) with a group of state attorneys general that had sued to challenge the company’s buyout of Warner Bros. Discovery, effectively paving the way for the mega merger to move forward, a person familiar with the matter told the AP.

U.K. charges man over alleged Rwanda genocide offences

​A 65-year-old Rwandan man has ‌been charged with genocide-related offences allegedly committed ⁠during the 1994 Rwandan Tutsi killings, British prosecutors said on ‌Monday (September 21, 2026).

Supreme Court orders fresh probe into 2012 rape-murder near Dharmasthala in Karnataka

The Supreme Court on Monday (September 21, 2026) ordered a fresh investigation into the 2012 brutal rape and murder of a 17-year-old near the bathing ghat on the outskirts of Dharmasthala in Karnataka while expressing shock at the botched-up probe into the incident.

Supreme Court judgment directs immediate release if arrested person is not provided with grounds of arrest, access to lawyer

The Supreme Court in a judgment on Monday (September 21, 2026) held that an arrested person kept in the dark about the grounds of arrest and without access to a lawyer was entitled to immediate release.

Supreme Court asks Tamil Nadu government to consider alternative site rather than evicting SASTRA varsity

The Supreme Court on Monday (September 21, 2026) asked the Tamil Nadu government to explore whether suitable alternative land was acceptable in lieu of government land allegedly encroached upon by SASTRA University in Thanjavur.

Class 10 girl and boy returning from coaching groped and assaulted in Bihar’s Jamui, sparking a political row

Two Class 10 students, a girl and a boy, returning from a coaching class, were allegedly groped and harassed by a group of men in Bihar’s Jamui district on Saturday (September 19, 2026). A video of the incident went viral on social media on Monday (September 21, 2026), prodding the police to register an FIR and arrest three people.

Namibian cheetah dies in M.P.’s Kuno National Park during treatment

Namibian cheetah Gaurav died in Madhya Pradesh’s Kuno National Park on Monday (September 21, 2026) evening while undergoing treatment, an official said. Ten-year-old Gaurav was rescued from the wild on September 12 after he was observed to be weak and dull.

Nilambur flash flood: five bodies recovered; search on for missing woman

Five bodies were recovered from the Kottapuzha River at T.K. Colony near Amarambalam, Nilambur, where a flash flood swept away visitors on Sunday (September 20, 2026) evening. Search operations continued throughout Monday (September 21, 2026) for Sajitha, a resident of T.K. Colony, who is still missing.

CSK names Zaheer Khan as head coach for IPL 2027

Chennai Super Kings (CSK) has appointed former India pacer Zaheer Khan as its head coach for IPL 2027. Zaheer replaces Stephen Fleming, who guided the Yellow Brigade from 2009 to 2026. The former New Zealand skipper was removed from the job earlier this year after three poor seasons for the five-time champion, in which it failed to qualify for the playoffs.

Asian Games | India and Sri Lanka tussle in yet another continental title clash

Nine days after facing off for continental dominance in the Asia Cup final in faraway Dubai, India and Sri Lanka will once again meet in another title clash, this time at the Asian Games in Nagoya on Tuesday (September 22, 2026).
